headline: Copy for your assistant

changes.title: Copy an item for your assistant
changes.now: Select an item and choose Copy, then For your assistant, at the top of its details, or press Ctrl+C when no text is selected. It copies the item's name, id, Jira key and how fresh the data is, so you can paste it into any assistant and ask, for example, how many of its stories are done.
changes.where: Copy at the top of an item's details, or Ctrl+C

changes.title: Copy with its details, or copy your stars
changes.now: Copy, then With its details (or Find) adds the item's record and, for an initiative, its story counts and stories, for an assistant that can't read files. Copy your starred items copies a reference for each star. Sticky notes are never copied.

changes.title: Assistants understand a pasted item
changes.now: The assistant instructions and the skills explain the reference Sightline copies, so an assistant finds the same item and says when its data may be older than yours.
changes.where: Connect assistant, Analyze with any assistant

changes.title: Starred outcomes and releases show their names
changes.now: A starred outcome or release is listed by its own name in Starred and in Find.
changes.before: They were listed as "meeting".
changes.where: Starred in the menu, and Find (/)

changes.title: One Copy menu on every item's details
changes.now: Copy at the top of an item's details holds Link, For your assistant and With its details, so the header stays on one line however narrow the panel or long the name.
changes.before: Copy link sat in the header on its own.
changes.where: Copy at the top of an item's details

headline: Find fixes

changes.title: Your stars stay near the top of Find
changes.now: With something selected, Find lists its five most used actions, then your stars, so they're in view without scrolling. Type > for every action.
changes.before: Eight actions for the selection could push your stars and recent items out of view.

changes.title: "zoom" finds Weeks and Days
changes.now: Typing "zoom" in Find (or "> zoom") offers Weeks view or Days view, as well as the time controls.
changes.before: Only the time controls came up.

headline: Find knows where you are

changes.title: Press / for what you'd do next
changes.now: Open Find with nothing typed and it starts with what fits where you are: actions for what you've selected (star it, update it, copy a link to it and more), your stars, what you opened recently, and this page's actions. If the selection changes while Find is open, its actions do nothing and say so.
changes.before: An empty Find listed only your stars.

changes.title: Recently opened items
changes.now: Find lists the last 8 items you opened, newest first, leaving out what's starred or selected. Back and Forward don't add to it. It's yours alone, kept in this browser for this plan; type "clear recent" in Find to forget it.

changes.title: Type > for actions only
changes.now: Start what you type in Find with > to see only actions, for example "> zoom". On its own, > lists every action that applies right now.

changes.title: Copy a link to the selection from Find
changes.now: With an item selected, type "copy link" in Find, or pick Copy a link to the selection under its name, to copy a link that opens it in this plan.

changes.title: Unstarring keeps your place in Starred
changes.now: After you unstar an item in Starred, the keyboard stays on the star now in its place.
changes.before: Focus jumped to the first star.

headline: Selected work stays out of the names

changes.title: Selected work and the Today line no longer cover the names
changes.now: When the chart is scrolled sideways, a selected initiative, task or milestone, and the red Today line, slide under the names column like everything else, so the names stay readable.
changes.before: A selected item that started before what's on screen was drawn over the names column, hiding the workstream's name and people, and in Days the Today line ran across the names.
changes.where: The Timeline, zoomed in or in Days, with something selected

headline: Stars

changes.title: Star anything to get back to it fast
changes.now: Select an item and press , (comma), or click the star at the top of its details, to star it. Your stars are under Starred in the menu and first in Find when you press / with nothing typed. Going to one shows it even if your filters hid it, and Back to where I was then puts your page, filters, zoom and scroll back as they were. Stars are yours alone, kept in this browser for this plan.
changes.where: The star at the top of an item's details, Starred in the menu, and Find (/)

changes.title: / no longer opens Find over a dialog
changes.now: Typing / while a dialog is open does nothing, so Find doesn't open behind it.
changes.before: / opened Find even with a dialog open.

headline: Linked work sideways

changes.title: See what shares a prerequisite
changes.now: While linked work is showing, open Linked work beside the chips and choose Work that waits for the same things. It adds the work held up by something your picks wait for, and what's in it, and the status line counts those items on their own. The same menu switches between Both ways and Leads here only, which used to be a separate button. Choose it again, or press Back, to take those items off.
changes.before: Show linked work showed what your picks wait for and what waits for them, but not other work held up by the same thing.
changes.where: The Linked work menu in the Showing strip, above the chart or the List

headline: Linked work counts what's shown

changes.title: The linked work count matches what's shown
changes.now: While linked work is showing, the status line counts only the linked items on screen, and says how many more your other filters hide, such as a person, a workstream, hidden done work or a tag. In the List, linked milestones and gates are said to be on the Timeline.
changes.before: The count included linked items your other filters hid, so it could say 6 when 3 were drawn.
changes.where: The status line, after Show linked work or Leads here only

headline: Long names in the List

changes.title: Long names wrap in the List
changes.now: A long initiative name wraps onto more lines in the List, so the table fits the window.
changes.before: When an initiative had tasks, a long name stayed on one line and the whole List had to be scrolled sideways.

headline: List status on one line

changes.title: Status stays on one line
changes.now: In the List, a status like Not started or In progress stays on one line, so rows keep their height and the other columns make room.
changes.before: On a laptop-width window, the Status column wrapped to two lines and doubled every row's height.

headline: See only what leads to a milestone

changes.title: Leads here only
changes.now: Show only what leads to the work you picked: everything it waits for, all the way back, and nothing that waits on it. Click Show on the Timeline under What leads here on a milestone's card, press > with an item selected, or click Leads here only beside the linked work chips. Both ways switches back, and Back undoes either.
changes.before: Linked work always showed both what an item waits for and what waits on it.
changes.where: A milestone's card, What leads here; or the chips above the Timeline while linked work is showing

changes.title: The > key
changes.now: With an item selected, > shows what leads to it on the Timeline. While linked work is showing, > switches between only what leads there and both ways. < still goes to What leads here on a milestone's card.

headline: Many more keyboard shortcuts

changes.title: Shortcuts for linked work, moves, rows and more
changes.now: C shows only what's linked to the selection, Shift+N moves it to the next sprint and { } move it a week. 0 shows all work. Shift+T opens the time controls, Shift+L goes to a milestone's What leads here, and Shift+W, Shift+O and Shift+E pick rows. Shift+C, Shift+X and Shift+Z work linked work. Press ? for the full list.
changes.before: Shift and a letter did the same as the letter alone, and these actions had no key.
changes.where: Press ? anywhere, or see each key beside its action in Find

changes.title: Switch off single-key shortcuts
changes.now: If letter keys get in the way of a screen reader or speech input, clear Single-key shortcuts at the top of the shortcuts page. Find and keys with Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) keep working.

headline: Faster redraws

changes.title: Faster redraws on big plans
changes.now: The page finds its own buttons and panels faster each time it redraws, so changes on a big plan show up sooner. Nothing looks or works differently.

headline: What's hidden, in one line

changes.title: Hidden-work notes fold into one line
changes.now: When the Timeline leaves things out for more than one reason, the notes under the toolbar now fold into one line that counts each reason, like "1 kind hidden · 1 initiative parked", with what you chose to hide first. Click Details for the full notes and their buttons; your browser remembers if you leave them open. One reason still shows in full, and warnings like the late count stay in view.
changes.before: Each reason had its own sentence, so several could stack above the chart.
changes.where: Timeline, the line under the toolbar, Details

headline: A quieter Timeline toolbar

changes.title: Time controls behind one button
changes.now: Weeks and Days, the sprint picker, the arrows, the presets and zoom now sit behind one Time button that says what's on screen, like "Time: Weeks · S2 (Oct 19 – Oct 30)". Click it to open them; your browser remembers if you leave them open. Shortcuts and Find work either way, and warnings like the late count stay in view.
changes.before: Every time control was always on the toolbar, next to View, Filters and Show.

headline: A milestone's runway

changes.title: What leads here
changes.now: A milestone's card now lists the work it waits for, all the way back: what finishes last and when, then the rest, latest first, with dates, status and owners. Anything finishing after the milestone's date is marked, and so are dates that come from Jira's sprints. Click an item to open it. Nothing here changes the plan.
changes.where: Select a milestone, What leads here

headline: The List, by connection

changes.title: By connection
changes.now: A new List layout puts each chain of linked work together, in the order it has to happen: what a row waits for comes before it. Chains go by when they start, a chain holding linked work you picked comes first, and work with no links is last. Copy as table keeps the groups.

headline: A quieter toolbar

changes.title: Connect assistant moves to your name menu
changes.now: Until an assistant is connected, Connect assistant waits in the menu under your name instead of the toolbar, and typing "assistant" in Find opens it too. Once one is connected, the toolbar shows its state as before: Assistant connected, paused, needs attention, or the changes waiting for your review.
changes.where: The menu under your name, top right

headline: Highlight linked work

changes.title: Highlight instead of hide
changes.now: While linked work is shown, click Highlight instead next to the chips (or use Find). Everything stays on the Timeline and in the List, and what isn't linked is dimmed. Dimmed work still works: hover, click or tab to it. Hide the rest switches back, and Back undoes either.
changes.where: The chips above the chart, Find, Timeline and List

changes.title: A shorter line for several picks
changes.now: With two or more picks, the status line counts them (Showing 3 picked items and the 10 linked to them) instead of repeating every title. The chips name them.

headline: Linked work for several items at once

changes.title: Pick up to 5 items
changes.now: While linked work is shown, select another initiative, task, milestone or gate and click Add to linked work (or use Find) to see what's linked to it too. Each pick gets its own chip, so you can take one off and keep the rest. Show linked work and Show only this initiative now sit together under the title, where you can see them.
changes.where: An item's details, Find and the chips above the chart

changes.title: The Key explains the dashed outline
changes.now: With an item selected, a dashed outline marks what it waits for or what waits for it directly. The Key now says so, and Fit includes a gate tied to the linked work.

headline: See what's linked to one item

changes.title: Show linked work
changes.now: Select an initiative, task, milestone or gate and click Show linked work, or use Find. You'll see that item, everything it waits for all the way back and everything that waits on it all the way on, with nothing else in the way, and the Timeline fits to all of it. A chip says what it's linked to; take it off, or press Back, to see the rest at your old zoom. The List shows the same work.
changes.where: An item's details, Find, Timeline and List

headline: Mac keys, shown as a Mac shows them

changes.title: ⌘, ⇧ and ⌥ on a Mac
changes.now: On a Mac, shortcuts read the way your keyboard is labeled: ⌘K for Find, ⌘S to save, ⇧⌘Z to redo and ⌥← to shorten. You'll see it in the keyboard help (?), next to actions in Find, in the toolbar's tooltips and in the status line's Undo hint. Other computers still show Ctrl, Shift and Alt.
changes.where: Keyboard help (?), Find and the toolbar

headline: J and K on the Plan pages

changes.title: Step through decisions, risks and cards
changes.now: On Milestones, Gates, Decisions and Risks, J and K (or the arrows, once you're on a row) step through the rows and read each one out, and Enter puts the cursor in its first field. On Cards they step through the cards, marking the whole card and bringing it into view, never stopping on its Jira link. While you're moving a card with M, they leave it alone.

headline: The assistant's check knows where each epic is

changes.title: Epic links are checked before they reach the page
changes.before: A connected assistant's check passed a link for an epic another initiative already held. The page then refused it, with a reason, when you went to apply it.
changes.now: The assistant's check refuses it up front and names where the epic is, so the change it proposes is one the page will take. An epic that's parked, or already where the change puts it, still passes.

headline: Link an epic from Find

changes.title: Link a Jira epic without the mouse
changes.now: With an initiative selected on the Timeline or the List, open Find and type link epic: the cursor lands in its epic box, with its section opened. Type the key and press Enter, and the cursor stays there for the next one.

changes.title: An epic counts on one initiative
changes.before: Typing an epic's key into a second initiative linked it there too. On an initiative with 50 epics, a 51st said Linked but wasn't kept. No earlier link was ever lost: only the new key, which never showed in the list.
changes.now: The epic box says which initiative already has that epic, and refuses a 51st with the reason. An epic parked on another initiative moves here instead. A connected assistant's epic links follow the same rules.
changes.where: An initiative's details, Organize, Jira epics

headline: Move the selection from Find

changes.title: A week later, a week earlier, or the next sprint
changes.now: With a task or initiative selected on the Timeline or the List, open Find and type week later, week earlier or next sprint. The status line says where it now starts, how many linked items moved with it, and that Ctrl+Z (⌘Z on a Mac) undoes it all. Focus stays on the item, so J, K and another move carry on. Jira-dated work isn't offered a move.

headline: Update it in Jira takes you there

changes.title: Update it in Jira opens the issue
changes.now: On Today, work whose dates come from Jira says Update it in Jira. When the plan knows your Jira site, that's now a link that opens the issue in a new tab.

changes.title: O says where it works
changes.before: Pressing O outside the Timeline and the List did nothing.
changes.now: It says O works on the Timeline and the List, so you know to select something there first.
changes.where: Any view other than the Timeline and the List

headline: Jira's dates hold everywhere

changes.title: Move all and Start today skip Jira's dates
changes.before: Move all on Today, and the Start today and +1 week buttons in an item's details, could move work whose dates come from its Jira sprint. The chart hid the move, but it was saved, and work waiting on it could really move.
changes.now: Move all counts and moves only work the plan dates, and says how many follow Jira sprints. Those buttons don't appear on work Jira dates. Nothing ever reached Jira. If you unlink such an item, check its dates.

changes.title: Moving an initiative leaves Jira's work inside it in place
changes.before: Moving an initiative also moved anything inside it whose dates come from Jira.
changes.now: What the plan dates moves with it; what Jira dates stays in its sprint.
changes.where: Timeline, initiatives with others inside them

changes.title: A change can't set what Jira owns right after linking it
changes.before: An assistant change that linked an epic and then set the same initiative's status or dates was accepted.
changes.now: It's refused with the reason, as it is for an initiative that was already linked.

headline: The arrow keys leave Jira's dates alone

changes.title: Arrow keys respect Jira's dates
changes.before: Left or Right on an item whose dates come from its Jira sprint saved a move the chart then hid, and really moved the plan's items that wait on it.
changes.now: The arrow keys leave it where it is and say to change its sprint in Jira, as dragging does. Nothing ever reached Jira. If you used them on a Jira item before, look in Activity for items that moved with it and set their dates back; Undo only works in the same session. If you later unlink such an item, check its dates.
changes.where: Timeline, a selected initiative or task linked to Jira

headline: O changes who owns the selection

changes.title: O for owners
changes.now: With a task or initiative selected on the Timeline or the List, press O to jump to its owner picker. Type a name and press Enter to add them; Undo takes it back. On a Jira item it sets the plan's lead, never Jira's assignee. Find offers it as Change who owns the selection.

changes.title: The owner picker's names stay in view
changes.before: Near the bottom of the details panel, the list of names an owner picker offered could open below the edge of the window.
changes.now: The list scrolls into view as it opens.
changes.where: Owner fields in the details panel

headline: I and X leave Jira's status alone

changes.title: I and X respect Jira
changes.before: On an item whose status comes from Jira, I or X still saved an update to the shared plan that Jira's status then overrode.
changes.now: I and X leave it unchanged, save nothing, and say the status comes from Jira. B for Blocked still works. Nothing ever reached Jira. A status saved this way before stays hidden behind Jira's while the item is linked; if you unlink it, check its status.
changes.where: Any selected task or initiative linked to Jira

changes.title: More room in the Roadmap idea mark
changes.now: The outline around the idea you moved to sits clear of its quarter buttons and the Drop link.

headline: The same "you are here" mark in every view, and Enter on a person

changes.title: One row mark everywhere
changes.before: On the Roadmap, the idea or deliverable you moved to with J or K had only a thin box around its name, and in People load only the name was marked.
changes.now: Roadmap ideas and deliverables, and a person's whole row of weeks in People load, get the same tint and outline as Today rows, clear of the text.

changes.title: Enter opens a person in People load
changes.now: Move to a person in People load with J or K, then press Enter to open their card. You stay on Capacity.

changes.title: Long titles end in an ellipsis
changes.before: A long title on Today was cut off mid-word with no sign there was more.
changes.now: It ends in an ellipsis, and pointing at it shows the whole title.

headline: J and K on the Roadmap, and arrows on Today, Sprint and Capacity

changes.title: J and K on the Roadmap
changes.now: J and K move through the Roadmap's deliverables and ideas. Enter opens the one you're on.

changes.title: Up and Down follow J and K
changes.now: Once you're on a row on Today, Sprint, Capacity or the Roadmap, the Up and Down arrows move to the next or previous one. From anywhere else on the page they scroll as usual.

changes.title: The row mark stays clear of text
changes.before: The outline on the row you moved to could cover the first letter of its text.
changes.now: The outline sits clear of the text on Today rows and People load names.

headline: J and K move through the view you're in

changes.title: J and K stay in the view you're in
changes.before: J and K always jumped to the Timeline first.
changes.now: J and K move to the next or previous item where you are. On the Timeline and List they select it; on Today, Sprint and Capacity they move focus, and Enter opens it. They go on from the item you're on, stop at either end, and a screen reader hears where you are, like 4 of 12.
changes.where: Today, Timeline, List, Sprint and Capacity

changes.title: J and K on rows by person
changes.before: With rows by person, J and K could pick an item that didn't exist and skip the rest.
changes.now: J and K reach each item on rows by person, including a task shared by two people, once on each of their rows.

headline: Run any action from Find

changes.title: Actions in Find
changes.before: Find looked up initiatives, tasks and people. An action you didn't know the key for meant hunting through menus.
changes.now: Press Ctrl+K or / and type what you want to do, like "days", "start editing", "rows by person" or "show only". Actions come first, each with its shortcut, and only the ones that apply right now are offered. Enter runs it.
changes.where: Find, at the top of the page (Ctrl+K or /)

changes.title: Shortcuts wait while you type
changes.before: A letter typed while an input method was composing, or in some rich text, could run a shortcut.
changes.now: Shortcuts stay quiet while you type anywhere, including while an input method is composing.

changes.title: Every shortcut is in the help
changes.now: The keyboard help (?) now lists T and L for Today and List, \ for the menu, and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo, which worked before but weren't listed.

headline: Back and Forward clear the last message

changes.title: Back and Forward clear the last message
changes.before: After Show all work, pressing Back brought your chips back while the line at the top still said all work was showing.
changes.now: Back and Forward clear the line at the top, so it never describes a step you've left.
changes.where: The line at the top of the page

headline: Show only, as chips you can take off

changes.title: Focus is now Show only, with chips
changes.before: Focus had levels, a path above the chart, a teammates' option that dimmed their tasks, and an automatic switch to Days, so it took a while to learn.
changes.now: Click Show only this initiative or Show Avery's work on a card, or press Z. A chip above the chart says what's shown: Initiative: Search, Person: Avery. Click a chip to take it off, or Show all work to clear every filter. Back undoes each step, and the zoom stays as it was.
changes.where: Timeline, List and Capacity: the card's Show only button, Z, or a double-click on an initiative

changes.title: The Filters count includes what you've shown only
changes.now: The number on Filters counts every filter, including the initiative or person you chose to show only, and a saved view keeps them.

changes.title: Show only tells you where the work is
changes.now: When nothing your chips show is in the dates on screen, a line under the chips says when that work is, and Go to it scrolls there without changing the zoom. If the chips match nothing at all, it says so, with Show all work beside it.
changes.where: The Showing strip above the Timeline

headline: Back and Forward keep your place

changes.title: Back puts you where you were
changes.before: Going back to a page brought back the item you had open, but the page, the chart and the details panel jumped to the top or drifted sideways.
changes.now: Back and Forward bring each page back as you left it: the same item open, and the page, the chart and the details panel scrolled where they were. Going back from one item to another puts the chart where the first one was. Links stay clean: scroll positions aren't in them.
changes.where: The browser's Back and Forward buttons, on every page

headline: Teammates' tasks stay readable while dimmed

changes.title: Dimmed, not faded
changes.before: With Show teammates' work on, teammates' tasks were drawn see-through, so in dark mode their names were hard to read.
changes.now: Teammates' tasks get a quiet outline with full-strength text, so they step back without fading out. The focused person's tasks keep their color.
changes.where: Focus on a person, then Show teammates' work

headline: Focus on one initiative or one person

changes.title: Focus, and step back out
changes.before: Seeing one initiative or one person's work took several steps in different places: Show only this, then the Days button, then a banner or the Filters panel to undo it.
changes.now: Press Focus on an initiative's or person's card, or select it and press Z. An initiative opens in Days by itself. Focus on a person inside it to see just their work there. The path above the chart steps back: click a step, press Esc, or Leave focus for the view you had.
changes.where: Timeline, List and Capacity: the Focus button on a card, or Z

changes.title: Teammates' work, when you want it
changes.now: While focused on a person, Show teammates' work on their initiatives adds everyone else's tasks there, dimmed so that person's work stays easy to pick out.
changes.where: The focus path above the chart

changes.title: A lead's initiative stays in their work
changes.before: Filtering to a person hid an initiative they lead when none of its tasks were theirs.
changes.now: It stays, with its tasks filtered as before.
changes.where: Filters > People, and Focus on a person

changes.title: Shortcuts on the one-line boxes
changes.now: Add an update and Add a note show their shortcuts, U and S, when you point at them, and screen readers announce them. An empty box you opened stays open until you reload the page.
changes.where: The details panel for an initiative or task

headline: Empty boxes take one line

changes.title: Updates and Notes stay small until you use them
changes.before: An item with no updates or notes still showed two empty text boxes, each with its own button, near the top of its details.
changes.now: Each empty box is one line with Add an update or Add a note. Click it, or press U or S, and the box opens with the cursor in it. A box with updates, notes or a half-written draft shows in full.
changes.where: The details panel for an initiative or task

headline: Clearer help when the page doesn't start

changes.title: Check a copy on Windows too
changes.before: When Sightline didn't start, the page said to check the copy with sha256sum, a command most Windows computers don't have.
changes.now: It now gives the command for Windows (Get-FileHash in PowerShell), a Mac and Linux, says to compare with the .sha256 file beside it, and says a mismatch means the file changed on the way over: copy it as a file, not by pasting its text.

changes.title: The whole message, with nothing over it
changes.before: When Sightline didn't start, the menu and an inactive toolbar still showed, and the menu covered the start of each line of the message.
changes.now: Only the message shows, so every step is readable.

headline: A lighter details panel

changes.title: What you need first, the rest folded
changes.before: An initiative's or task's details showed every field at once, so you scrolled past schedule, links and setup to find what you needed.
changes.now: Warnings, status, updates, notes, title, owner, dates and the first three tasks come first. Schedule, Waits for, Organize and More fold away, each with a one-line summary such as "2 weeks". The folds you open are remembered for initiatives and tasks, in this browser.

headline: A lighter menu

changes.title: Pin the pages you use, and the rest folds away
changes.before: The menu showed every page in every group at once, with a count beside most of them.
changes.now: Your pinned pages sit at the top: Today, Sprint, Timeline and Capacity to start. Groups start closed and show a dot when something inside needs you. Numbers show only when something needs you, such as high risks. Delivery is split into Plan, Review and History.
changes.where: The menu on the left. Point at a page and click the pin, or focus it and press P. Up to five, in this browser only.

headline: Task names stay on screen in Days

changes.title: Names near the right edge are no longer cut off
changes.before: In Days, the name of a short task or a milestone near the right edge ran past the edge of the chart and was cut off.
changes.now: A task name that won't fit to the right of its bar sits to its left instead. If neither side has room, it is shortened with an ellipsis. Milestone names near the edge are shortened the same way. Point at a shortened name to see it in full.
changes.where: Days, especially with one initiative open

headline: No new version without a change

changes.title: Saving with nothing changed leaves the file alone
changes.before: Done editing always saved, so the shared file got a new revision and a new save time even when you changed nothing. Save, and a quick update that changed nothing, did the same.
changes.now: The file only changes when the plan does. Done editing with nothing changed puts the file back exactly as it was before Start editing. Save, and quick updates, with nothing changed write nothing. An edit you changed back counts as nothing.
changes.where: Start editing, Save, Done editing, and quick updates on a shared plan

headline: Old captures show on Today

changes.title: Captures waiting over 30 days show on Today
changes.before: A request or idea nobody handed off or declined stayed in To triage, on the Roadmap, however old it got.
changes.now: In the Team view, Today lists captures open for over 30 days under Waiting in triage, oldest first, with who asked and how long it's been open. Needs attention counts them. Triage opens one in To triage, to hand it off or decline it.

headline: Tasks that start too early are counted

changes.title: Tasks that start too early are in the warning bar
changes.before: A task that started before what it waits for finished was tagged too early on the Days view, but the warning bar and Present's review only counted initiatives.
changes.now: Open tasks that start too early are listed with initiatives in the warning bar, among work that starts before what it waits for finishes. Click a name to open it, or Move them later to fix them all. In Present, Review counts them as starting too early, and stepping through them opens each task.
changes.where: The warning bar above the chart, and Review in Present

changes.title: Finished tasks keep their dates
changes.before: Move them later, and automatic moving, could push a done task later when what it waited for ran late, rewriting when the work happened.
changes.now: A done task stays on the dates it ran on. Only open work moves.
changes.where: Move them later, and automatic moving of linked work

headline: See only what was added here

changes.title: Show only work added here
changes.before: You could show only Jira's work, but not the reverse: the work your team added that nothing in Jira tracks.
changes.now: Added here, next to All sources, Jira only and Jira + mine, shows only tasks and initiatives with no Jira key, plus any initiative holding such work. Jira-linked items and Jira's stories are hidden; milestones, gates and notes stay. A banner says so, Present too. It's your own choice, for this plan in this browser.

headline: Waits-for links merge link by link

changes.title: Two people adding what something waits for both keep their links
changes.before: When you and a teammate both changed what the same task or initiative waits for, their links won and yours went to a backup.
changes.now: Both sets of links are kept, and a link one of you removed stays removed. A link that would make work wait for itself through the other person's links isn't merged: theirs wins, yours is backed up, and Sightline tells you which link wasn't kept.
changes.where: Saving a shared plan someone else changed

headline: Line up existing tasks behind what they wait for

changes.title: Move a task to right after what it waits for
changes.before: Your assistant could add a task after others, but couldn't move a task that was already in the plan there. It could only guess a date, without your holidays and time off.
changes.now: A proposed move can say start after instead of a date. The task starts the working day after the last thing it waits for finishes, skipping weekends, holidays and its owners' time off. It keeps its id and its links. When something it waits for is late and not done, it's refused: give a date.
changes.where: Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

changes.title: Marking existing tasks as guesses no longer conflicts
changes.before: A proposed change marking a task's length as a guess was refused as changed since you looked, on every task that wasn't marked yet.
changes.now: A task that isn't marked as a guess reads as not a guess, so the change applies.
changes.where: Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

headline: Order without dates

changes.title: See the work in order, without dates
changes.now: By order, in the List, groups work into steps: step 1 waits for nothing, and each later step waits only on earlier ones. Waiting for an initiative means waiting for everything in it. Steps show order, not what's ready. Loops, and waiting and unstaffed rows, are set apart. The Waits on column is now Waits for.

changes.title: Capacity says what it doesn't count
changes.before: Capacity counted story points in Jira, so work with no estimate, or work added here, quietly didn't show up in it.
changes.now: Under the capacity table, a line says what the points leave out in those sprints: Jira items with no estimate, and open tasks added here.

headline: Clearer about what's what

changes.title: Added here, on work Jira doesn't track
changes.before: Work typed into the plan looked much like Jira work, so a rough idea could be read as tracked, committed work.
changes.now: In a plan that has Jira work, plan tasks on the Days view and rows in the List that nothing in Jira tracks say Added here. On the Timeline, an initiative with no Jira key says so when you hover it, and the Key explains it. A plan with no Jira work shows no labels.
changes.where: Days view, List, and the Timeline's Key

changes.title: Moved dates say what they wait for
changes.before: A proposed change listed each date it moved, but not why it might have moved.
changes.now: Each date a proposed change moves later now says what that item waits for, like waits for "Adapter". Holidays, time off and gates can move dates too, so it says what it waits for, not that it moved because of it.
changes.where: Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

changes.title: Apply says what it added
changes.now: After you apply proposed changes, the status line counts what changed, like 30 tasks added, 29 links added, 12 dates moved. Your assistant reads the same count.

headline: Order before dates

changes.title: Add tasks by what they start after
changes.before: Every task needed a start date, so a plan whose order was known but not its dates got the same placeholder date on every task.
changes.now: A proposed task can say what it starts after instead of a date. It starts the working day after the last of those finishes, skipping weekends, holidays and its owners' time off. The review says what each starts after.
changes.where: Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

changes.title: Mark a length as a guess
changes.now: Length is a guess, on a task's card, hatches the task on the Days view and labels it guess. The initiative's card counts how many of its tasks have guessed lengths.
changes.where: A task's card, under its dates

changes.title: Start right after what it waits for
changes.now: A task that could start sooner says so on its card, with the day and a link to start then. One that starts before what it waits for finishes is flagged on its card and tagged too early on the Days view. The card also says whether it moves later on its own.
changes.where: A task's card, under its dates

headline: Show only some initiatives

changes.title: Show only one or more initiatives
changes.before: Only the Day view focused on one initiative. Elsewhere, narrowing the plan meant filtering by workstream, person or tag.
changes.now: Show only this, on an initiative's card, narrows Timeline, List and Capacity to it, everything inside it and what holds it. Also show this adds more. Milestones done when a shown initiative is stay; gates are hidden. The picks are a filter like the others, so a saved view keeps them.
changes.where: An initiative's card, or Filters, Initiatives

headline: Dates in words

changes.title: Give dates the way people say them
changes.before: Every date in an assistant's proposed change had to be YYYY-MM-DD, so "start it next Monday" had to be worked out first.
changes.now: Any date in a proposed change can be words like tomorrow, +3d, next Friday, 2 weeks ago or next sprint. The review says which date each became, flags one in the past, and says when a task's start moves off a weekend. Apply uses that date. Anything else is refused with the forms that work.
changes.where: Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

headline: Who asked, and what happened since

changes.title: See captures by who asked, and send them a note
changes.before: To triage grouped open captures by workstream only, so answering "what happened to the things we raised?" meant opening each one.
changes.now: By asker lists everything each person or group raised, open ones first, then what became of the rest. Copy a note for them copies a short note to send back, saying where each one stands. It names no one else.

changes.title: A meeting recap of what changed
changes.now: Meeting recap says what's new, raised again, closed and reopened since your last meeting, and how many are still open, ready to read out or paste. It leaves out who asked unless you tick Say who asked.

headline: Raised again, not captured twice

changes.title: Record that a request came up again
changes.before: When a request came up in a second meeting, it was captured again or not at all, so nobody could see how often it was asked for.
changes.now: A capture's card lists every later time it was raised: who asked, which meeting and when. Record it adds one, and Remove takes one out. The first ask stays as it was. Plans with these records open read-only in older copies of Sightline, so everyone editing should update first.
changes.where: Roadmap, To triage, open a capture: Raised again

changes.title: The capture form offers the one you may already have
changes.now: As you type what was raised, the form lists captures with a similar name. Same thing: record it there adds this meeting to that one; Capture keeps it separate. Nothing is merged on its own.
changes.where: Add (or A, then C), Capture a request or idea

changes.title: To triage shows how often something comes up
changes.now: A capture raised more than once says so in its row, like raised 3 times. Hover over it to see when and by whom.

changes.title: Your assistant records repeats instead of capturing twice
changes.now: With the meeting-to-plan skill, a request that matches a capture already in the plan is proposed as raised again on that one. When it isn't sure, it captures it separately and says which one it may repeat.

headline: Capture in one step

changes.title: Capture a request or idea in one step, even mid-meeting
changes.before: Capturing by hand took two steps: add a roadmap idea, then set Captured as, Asked by and Raised on on its card.
changes.now: One short form: what was raised, its type, who asked, the workstream, the meeting and its date. Only what was raised is needed; nothing else is guessed. The meeting and date carry over, and Capture and add another keeps the form open.
changes.where: Add (or A, then C) and Capture a request or idea; Roadmap, To triage

changes.title: The roadmap's add row says what it's for
changes.before: New idea and Capture sat side by side with nothing saying which to use.
changes.now: The row at the top is New roadmap idea, + Add to the roadmap, for something you might ship. A line under it sends requests and questions someone raised to Capture, so they wait in To triage with who asked.

headline: A capture closes one way, and held changes say why

changes.title: A captured item is either handed off or declined, not both
changes.before: An assistant's proposal, or two people at once, could hand off a declined item or decline a handed-off one, leaving it both.
changes.now: Handing off or declining a closed item is refused until it's reopened. If two people close it differently at the same time, its card says both and asks you to reopen it and close it once.
changes.where: Roadmap, To triage; the item's card

changes.title: A change that waits for you says the right reason
changes.before: A change that added a person, group or skill waited for review with the reason "It deletes an initiative with Jira-linked work".
changes.now: It says what it does: adds a person, a group or a skill, deletes a workstream or changes a workstream's ID.

headline: Tags on short bars show whole or not at all

changes.title: A late or +1 tag is never cut off on a short bar
changes.before: On short bars, especially at Fit, a tag that didn't fit was cut mid-word, so late showed as "lat" or "la".
changes.now: A tag shows whole, or not at all when the bar is too short for it. Late bars keep their red outline, and screen readers still hear late and every owner.

headline: Capture what comes up in meetings

changes.title: Capture requests, ideas, gaps and questions, and triage them
changes.before: Things raised in meetings that weren't work yet could only go in as roadmap ideas, with no record of who asked or what became of them.
changes.now: A roadmap item can be captured as a request, idea, process gap or question, with who asked, the meeting's date and its source. To triage lists open captures by workstream, oldest first. Hand one off to an initiative or a Jira issue, or decline it with a reason; neither marks anything done.
changes.where: Roadmap, To triage; the item's card

changes.title: Assistants can capture from meeting notes, and new people and groups always wait for you
changes.before: An assistant could add a person or a skill on its own at the levels that apply routine changes.
changes.now: Your assistant can capture each item from your meeting notes with who asked. A new person, group or skill always waits for your review, whatever it may do on its own.

headline: Ask any assistant about your plan

changes.title: Instructions any assistant can follow to analyze your plan
changes.before: Assistant instructions were written for a connected private folder, so an assistant that couldn't read your files, like a chat window, had nothing to go on.
changes.now: Analyze with any assistant copies read-only instructions for Copilot, ChatGPT or any other assistant, copies them together with the plan's data for one that can't read files, or saves them as AGENTS.md to put beside your plan. Notes are left out, and nothing is changed.
changes.where: Connect assistant, then Analyze with any assistant

headline: Assistants see what each change does

changes.title: Every change an assistant can propose comes with a plain description
changes.before: The context file listed each change an assistant could propose by its name and arguments only, so an assistant had to guess what some of them did.
changes.now: Each change in the context file now has a one-line description of what it does. The planning skills tell the assistant to choose by that description and use the arguments exactly.
changes.where: The assistant folder's context file, and the bundled planning skills

headline: Owner initials stay clear of names

changes.title: Three-letter owner initials no longer cover the name on a short bar
changes.before: On a short bar, three-letter initials, or a wide system font, could make the owner's circle wider than the space kept for it, so the end of the name ran underneath.
changes.now: Three-letter initials are set slightly smaller, and the circle on a bar never grows past its space, so the name always stops before it.
changes.where: Weeks and Days, on Jira stories and tasks

headline: See who owns each Jira item at a glance

changes.title: Owner initials on every Jira item
changes.before: Who owned a Jira story showed as plain text in some places, as initials in others, and not at all on most bars.
changes.now: Every Jira item shows its owner as a small circle with their initials, at the right end of bars and on tiles, cards, List rows and details. A dashed empty circle means unassigned; an outlined one is an owner outside the team. Hover for the full name. People who share initials get a third letter. No pictures are fetched.
changes.where: Timeline (Weeks and Days), sprint shelves, Cards, List, and the details panel

changes.title: Spotlight rings the person's circles
changes.now: With Spotlight on from the Show menu, that person's owner circles get a ring wherever they appear, so their work stands out on bars as well as on the shelves.

headline: List shows workstreams

changes.title: A By workstream layout
changes.before: List could group work by initiative or by person, but not by workstream, so the rows you see on Timeline had no match in List.
changes.now: By workstream shows each workstream in its Timeline order, with its color, its initiatives and their tasks under it, and a count. List now opens this way unless you picked a different layout on this plan before; choose By initiative once and List remembers it. Copy as table keeps the groups. Everything by start date is now called By start date.
changes.where: List, the layout buttons at the top

changes.title: A Workstream column
changes.now: Every row now says which workstream it's in, on screen and in Copy as table. By workstream leaves the column out, since each group already names it. Like the other columns, you can resize it or set it to wrap.

headline: Names stay in view as you scroll the timeline

changes.title: Bars keep their names when their start is off the screen
changes.before: Scrolling the timeline sideways cut a bar's name at the left edge, so a bar that started off the screen showed only the end of its name.
changes.now: A bar's name rides along the left edge of the chart for as long as any of the bar shows. Where only part of the bar is on screen, the name is shortened with an ellipsis inside the bar and never covers the next one. Hover or a screen reader still gives the whole name.
changes.where: Timeline, in Weeks, zoomed to a few sprints

changes.title: Milestone, gate and stretch labels follow too
changes.now: When a milestone, gate or stretch marker is just off to the left, its label stays at the left edge with ‹ in place of the marker, until its own space scrolls away. Printing shows every label where it starts.

headline: Jira stories stay with their epic when the epic has a parent

changes.title: Stories group under their epic, not the initiative above it
changes.before: When the plan linked an epic that has its own parent in Jira (an initiative above it), that epic's stories were filed under the initiative instead. In a sprint, not on the board listed them as loose work missing a parent, and Sort Jira work grouped them under the initiative.
changes.now: Stories group under their epic again, the same as when the epic isn't linked in the plan. After you update, some stories move from the loose list and the initiative's group into their epic's group. Nothing in the plan file changes. An epic inside another epic still rolls up to the top epic.
changes.where: Work, Sort Jira work, and the In a sprint, not on the board list

headline: The side panel stays where you were

changes.title: Buttons in the side panel no longer jump it back to the top
changes.before: Clicking a button partway down the side panel, such as Copy files or Approve in the assistant panel, or a status in an initiative's panel, scrolled the panel back to the top every time.
changes.now: The panel stays where you were after a click. Opening a different item still starts at the top.
changes.where: The panel on the right: the planning assistant, and any item you open

headline: Calmer story shelves on the timeline

changes.title: Story shelf labels fit in two short lines
changes.before: The label beside a workstream's Jira stories wrapped to six lines or more, with a Spotlight list and a note that could spill over the chart, so the row grew tall around a few small summaries.
changes.now: The label reads Jira and the story count, then points, done and not estimated on a second line. Hover it for the whole summary; screen readers hear all of it. A small button beside it switches between tiles and summaries. A shelf with nothing on screen takes one line.

changes.title: Zoomed in, only the sprints on screen open
changes.before: At one or two sprints, every sprint's stories opened as tiles, so a sprint scrolled out of view could make a row tall and empty.
changes.now: Only the sprints in view show tiles; the rest stay as one-line summaries. Click a summary, or the button beside the label, to open them all. Stories with no sprint sit on their own strip under the sprints.
changes.where: Timeline, This sprint or This + next

changes.title: Spotlight is one choice for the whole chart
changes.before: Each workstream had its own Spotlight list next to its stories.
changes.now: Pick a person once, under Spotlight a person in the Show menu, and their stories stay lit on every shelf while the rest dim. Each name shows how many stories they have, and each shelf's label gives their count there.
changes.where: Timeline, Show, then Spotlight a person

changes.title: What tile sizes mean is in the Key
changes.now: The note that tiles are sized by points, and that a tile's place in a sprint says nothing about when, is said once, in the Key, instead of beside every shelf.

headline: Cards: the plan's Jira work, by workstream

changes.title: A Cards page for the plan's Jira work
changes.before: Jira stories on the plan were only bars on the timeline or rows under their initiative, and the Sprint page showed just the current sprint.
changes.now: Cards shows every Jira story, task and one-issue initiative on the plan as a card. Rows are workstreams in plan order, with cards grouped under their initiative and the rest last. Columns are status (to do, in progress, done, and canceled when you ask) or sprint (earlier, the active one, the next ones, no sprint). Rows can also be people or epics.

changes.title: Filters and honest totals
changes.now: Filter by sprint, person, status, epic or text, or click Mine. Each row and the whole board count cards and estimated points, and say how many aren't estimated, how many you hid, and how many the filters leave out, each on its own.

changes.title: Move a card to place it in the plan
changes.now: Drag a card to another workstream or onto an initiative to place it there, the same way Sort Jira work does, with Undo. Without a mouse, press M on a card, choose the place with the arrow keys, and press Enter. The card glides to where it lands.

changes.title: Move a card across columns to propose a change
changes.now: Dropping a card on another status or sprint doesn't change Jira. It makes a Jira change proposal, and the card shows it as proposed. When a column covers several of your workflow's statuses, you pick which one. Your last pick is remembered.

changes.title: Choose what a card shows
changes.now: Choose the fields a card shows and their order (key, summary, status, assignee, points, sprint, epic, parent, labels, priority, due date, blocked, initiative), compact, normal or detailed, and wider cards for more points. The plan holds the team's layout; you can use your own in this browser, with Reset to the team's layout.

changes.title: Hide a Jira item, with a reason
changes.now: Hide a card to keep it off the plan's views, with an optional reason. Sightline uses the plan's own ways: a story is switched off in its initiative, an epic is parked, an issue not on the plan is marked not ours. The Hidden list shows how and why, with Bring back. Work that's on the plan as its own task or initiative can't be hidden.

changes.title: The assistant can set the card layout and hide items
changes.now: An assistant can change the team's card layout and hide or bring back Jira items. Each change waits for your review, which says how each item would be hidden, including when hiding parks an epic.

changes.title: Older copies open these plans read-only
changes.now: A plan with a team card layout or hide reasons opens read-only in an older copy of Sightline, so nothing is lost. Update everyone's copy to edit it.

headline: Days opens and scrolls smoothly in big plans

changes.title: Days lays out only the rows near the screen
changes.before: Days laid out every initiative's row at once, so in a large plan it took several seconds to open and scrolling stuttered.
changes.now: The rows near the screen are laid out first and the rest as you scroll to them. In a large plan Days opens in about a third of the time and scrolls smoothly. Every row is still on the page, so finding text and printing work as before.

headline: Opening and closing an item is quicker

changes.title: Choosing an item no longer redraws the whole timeline
changes.before: Clicking an initiative, task, Jira story or milestone, or closing its panel with Esc, ×, or Done, redrew the whole timeline just to move the highlight. In a large plan that took about two seconds.
changes.now: The timeline stays as it is and only the highlight and its links move, so in a large plan opening an item takes about 75% less time and closing it about 85% less. Anything that changes what the timeline shows, like an edit, a filter, a new day or a folded sprint shelf, still redraws it in full.

headline: Sprint presets answer in half the time

changes.title: Presets draw the timeline once
changes.before: Choosing This sprint, This + next, Next 3 or Fit, by button or with Shift and a number, drew the whole timeline twice.
changes.now: It's drawn once, so in a large plan a preset takes about half as long. The preset is still remembered for your next visit.

headline: The Timeline answers faster with sprint shelves on

changes.title: Sprint shelves no longer slow every click
changes.before: With sprint shelves on, each redraw worked out every story's sprint from scratch, so in a large plan zooming, filtering, opening an item and Undo all took several seconds.
changes.now: The shelves work out the sprints once per workstream. In a large plan, Fit and zooming are about 40% faster, This + next about 25%, and opening an item, filtering, Undo and saving about 25 to 30%. The shelves look the same.
changes.where: Timeline, in Weeks with sprint shelves on

headline: Big plans draw faster, Days most of all

changes.title: Note counts no longer slow every redraw
changes.before: Each time the page redrew, every item checked every note to find its own, so a plan with many notes and items was slow everywhere, and Days, which shows the most items, was slowest.
changes.now: Notes are sorted by item once per redraw. In a large plan, Days opens in about half the time, opening the plan is about 13% faster, and changing the Timeline's zoom, a preset or a filter is about 10% faster. The note counts and badges are the same as before.
changes.where: Everywhere items show a note count, most noticeably Days

headline: The timeline's header is short again

changes.title: Zoom controls moved to the toolbar
changes.before: The sprint picker, the 1, 2, 3 and Fit presets, − and + and the dates on screen were stacked in the timeline's top-left corner, pushing the first row down by about six lines.
changes.now: They're one compact group in the toolbar, beside Weeks and Days: ‹ the sprint picker › | 1 2 3 Fit | − +. Tooltips keep the full names and shortcuts, and the picker's tooltip shows the dates on screen. The corner holds just the row label again.

headline: Jira stories on sprint shelves, sized by points

changes.title: Sprint shelves for Jira stories
changes.before: In Weeks, every Jira story in a sprint was drawn as its own full-width bar, so a busy workstream became a wall of identical bars that said nothing about size or status.
changes.now: Each workstream's Jira stories sit on a shelf per sprint, grouped under their initiative. A tile's width follows its points, on one scale for the whole chart, and it shows its points, a status symbol, and who has it. Not estimated stories get their own strip, and stories with no sprint are counted as Unscheduled. Nothing in the plan changes.

changes.title: Honest shelf summaries
changes.now: Each shelf sums its stories, estimated points and done points, next to the stories not estimated. It says when filters apply, and that capacity isn't compared yet.

changes.title: Summaries at Fit, tiles at one sprint
changes.now: At Fit or several sprints, each shelf shows a short summary. Pick one or two sprints to see the tiles. Show the stories, beside a workstream's shelves, opens or folds them by hand, and that choice is kept in this browser.

changes.title: Spotlight one person
changes.now: Pick a person in Spotlight to light up their tiles across the shelves, with their stories, points and stories not estimated.
changes.where: Timeline, the shelf row's label, while the stories show

changes.title: Go back to bars if you prefer
changes.now: Show, then On sprint shelves, turns the shelves off and draws each story as a bar again. Days keeps its story rows either way.

headline: Size List's columns, and choose which ones wrap

changes.title: Resize any column
changes.before: List's columns sized themselves to their text, so a long name or a long list of waits could squeeze everything else.
changes.now: Drag the edge of a column's heading to resize it, or focus the edge and use the arrow keys. Double-click an edge for its default width. Wide tables scroll sideways.

changes.title: Choose which columns wrap
changes.now: Columns, in List's toolbar, sets each column to wrap or keep one line. A one-line column is cut short and shows the full text on hover. Reset columns puts everything back. These settings are yours, in this browser, and printing still shows every column in full.

changes.title: Item names are full size
changes.before: Item names in List were drawn smaller than the other columns, and their cells didn't line up with the rest of the row.
changes.now: Item names use the same size as the rest of the table, and every cell in a row lines up.

headline: Change a workstream's ID so it says what the workstream is

changes.title: A workstream's ID can be changed
changes.before: A workstream kept its first ID forever, so after a rename or a restructure the ID could say something else.
changes.now: Change it in the workstream's panel, under ID. Everything that uses it changes in the same update: work, milestones, notes, meetings, process blocks, deliverables, time splits, guidance, saved views, the baseline, snapshots and the last status update. One Undo puts it all back.
changes.where: Click a workstream's name on the Timeline, then ID

changes.title: Assistants can propose an ID change, and you always review it
changes.now: An assistant can propose a workstream's new ID. It always waits for you, at every review level. A change an assistant wrote before the ID changed still applies: review says it used the old ID.

changes.title: Old IDs keep working
changes.now: The plan remembers a workstream's old IDs, so files and copies that still use them find it, and an old ID is never given to another workstream. Older versions of Sightline open a plan with a changed ID read-only.

headline: See one whole sprint, edge to edge, and step sprint by sprint

changes.title: Fit the view to a sprint
changes.before: "1 sprint" showed a sprint's width wherever the view happened to be, so it usually showed parts of two sprints, and the arrows moved by screens, not sprints.
changes.now: Pick a sprint in the zoom control and the view fits it exactly, from its first day to its last, in Weeks and Days, for sprints of any length. The arrows and [ and ] step whole sprints, and . goes to the sprint we're in. Show two or more sprints with + and −. The choice stays in this browser and links carry it.
changes.where: Timeline, the zoom control at the top left

changes.title: One click to this sprint, the next two, or the next three
changes.before: The Timeline opened on Fit, and getting to this sprint and the next meant clicking + many times.
changes.now: This sprint, This + next, Next 3 and Fit sit beside the sprint picker, each fitted from the sprint we're in (or the next one, between sprints). Shift+1, Shift+2, Shift+3 and Shift+0 do the same. A plan with sprints opens on This + next the first time, then on your last choice. A link with a sprint still wins.
changes.where: Timeline, the zoom control at the top left

headline: Milestone and gate labels that fall close together stay readable

changes.title: Labels close together no longer run into each other
changes.before: On Weeks, milestone, gate, release and note labels were spaced by a rough guess of their width, so at some zooms, window widths and text sizes neighbors overlapped and couldn't be read.
changes.now: Labels are spaced by their real width at the chart's current zoom, width and text size, and spaced again when any of those change. A workstream's milestones use three rows at most; past that, a label is cut short where the next one starts, keeping its date, and shows in full when you hover over it or tab to it. Gates whose markers would touch share one flag, with a count.

headline: Install Sightline with npm

changes.title: One command to install
changes.before: Getting Sightline meant cloning the source and building it.
changes.now: npx @troylar/sightline install <folder> puts the app, the planning skills and an invented example plan in a new folder. The README and the availability page explain each install route.

changes.title: Helpers match the app they came with
changes.before: The package's Jira sync and assistant helpers weren't stamped with the app's version, so they didn't match the copies the app hands out.
changes.now: sightline helpers points to helpers stamped with the app's version, the same files the app and its download carry.

changes.title: Neutral wording for any assistant
changes.now: The instructions the app gives your AI assistant use a generic source name and batch id in their example. Any assistant's name is still accepted and shown as written.

headline: Stories under a feature are sorted under their epic

changes.title: A story under a feature groups under its epic
changes.before: When Jira had a feature between an epic and its stories, a story the epic's list didn't include (its epic not on the plan, or the story not in a sprint) was grouped under the feature, often with no name, or shown with No epic.
changes.now: It's grouped under the first epic above it, with the epic's name, in the list and in In a sprint, not on the board.

changes.title: Says when it can't trace stories to their epic
changes.now: If the sync didn't find Jira's Parent Link field, it says so after each run, and Sort Jira work explains why stories under a feature show with No epic and how to check.
changes.where: The sync's output, and Work, then Sort Jira work

headline: See where we are: the sprint we're in and today, on every timeline

changes.title: The sprint we're in is shaded, and its header says now
changes.before: Nothing on the chart showed which sprint was the current one.
changes.now: A soft band runs behind the bars for the sprint we're in, and its header reads, for example, "Sprint 42 · now". Between sprints there's no band, the next sprint's header says when it starts, and the line above the chart says we're between sprints.

changes.title: Today has a line and a Today tab in both zooms
changes.before: Weeks had a line with no label, and Days only tinted today's column.
changes.now: A red line marks today, with a Today tab in the time header. In Weeks it sits at today inside the week. When today is before or after the plan's dates, the tab waits at that edge with the date.

changes.title: Jump to today works in Weeks too
changes.before: Pressing . always switched to Days.
changes.now: Pressing . keeps your zoom: in Weeks it scrolls to the sprint we're in, or the next one between sprints.

changes.title: Now shows in the load grid and the roadmap
changes.now: The load grid marks the sprint's weeks and this week, and the roadmap marks the quarter we're in.

changes.title: Sprint names keep their space
changes.before: A sprint called "Sprint 42" showed as "Sprint42" in the timeline header.
changes.now: Sprint names show as written.

headline: An update that keeps being overwritten no longer saves over and over

changes.title: Putting back an overwritten update can't loop
changes.before: When something kept restoring an older copy of the plan file, such as another open copy or a sync tool, the page put the update back again and again, saving every couple of seconds without end. A change that read back slightly differently could do the same with nobody else involved.
changes.now: An overwritten update is put back once. If the file changes back again, Sightline stops, downloads your version as a backup, and says what to check, naming whoever saved the file last when the file says. A file that still holds exactly what you saved is never saved again.
changes.where: Any quick update to a shared plan

headline: Assistant changes apply whole, or say why not

changes.title: A change no longer lands only partly
changes.before: An assistant change that moved an initiative earlier and made it longer could apply only the longer part: the plan's scheduling put the start back, because it waits on something that ends later, and nothing said so.
changes.now: The change waits instead, and review says why: it would start on the later date because it waits on the named item. Change what it waits on, or move that first. A change the schedule allows still applies whole, with one undo.

headline: Settings pages that say where you are, and a File menu for files

changes.title: Plan details has its own page
changes.before: The plan's start date, sprint length, automatic moves and Jira link address were behind File, then Plan settings.
changes.now: Settings, then Plan details shows them, with Edit plan details to change them.

changes.title: Every Settings page is titled with its name
changes.before: Some pages had no title, or one that didn't match the menu, like Jira for Jira connection.
changes.now: Each page starts with its name exactly as the menu says it, and the menu's group names (Plan, Team, Connections) are read out by screen readers.

changes.title: File holds only file actions
changes.before: File also had Jira setup, Plan settings, Set baseline and Start with.
changes.now: File has the shared file, importing a copy and exporting one. Set baseline is on Delivery, then Snapshots, and Start Sightline with is in the menu at the right of the header. Jira setup is Settings, then Jira connection.

headline: Text size, and a tidier header

changes.title: Make the text larger or smaller
changes.now: Choose A+ or A− to change the page's text from 90% to 150% in 10% steps, without browser zoom, and Reset to go back to 100%. Text never gets smaller than 9 pixels. The size stays in this browser and isn't saved in the plan.
changes.where: The menu at the right of the header, under Text size

changes.title: You, theme, what's new and help in one menu
changes.before: Who you are, the theme, What's new and Help were four separate buttons across the top.
changes.now: One button at the right of the header shows your initials, or Choose yourself, and opens a menu with who you are, text size, theme, What's new and help. A dot on it means there's something new to read.

changes.title: View says how you're looking at the plan
changes.before: The rows and sources choices took up most of the bar above the chart.
changes.now: View holds the rows (by workstream, person or epic) and the sources, and the button says what's chosen, like View: By person · Jira only. R still switches rows.

headline: What each workstream is for, and skills on the team

changes.title: See what a workstream is for
changes.now: Point at a workstream's name, or move to it with the keyboard, to see its description with headings, lists and links, who works in it and what it holds. An item's panel links to its workstream's description, and the workstream's panel lets you edit it.
changes.where: Workstream names in Weeks and Days, and the item panel

changes.title: Skills on people and on work
changes.now: Keep a list of the skills your team cares about, give people theirs, and say which skills an initiative or task needs. Renaming a skill keeps it everywhere, and a skill still in use can't be removed until it's taken off.
changes.where: Settings, then Team, and each person's, initiative's and task's panel

changes.title: Milestones get a story
changes.now: Write what a milestone marks and when it's reached, in Markdown, from a template you can change. Gates get a description the same way. Both show when you point at them.
changes.where: The milestone or gate panel, and Settings for the template

changes.title: Notes for your assistant
changes.now: Leave a short note for your assistant on people, work, milestones, gates, deliverables, decisions and risks. It sits under For the assistant, closed, and is only ever advice: it can't approve or authorize a change. Anyone who can open the plan, and your assistant's provider, can read it.

changes.title: Your assistant can keep descriptions and skills up to date
changes.before: Your assistant couldn't change workstream guidance, skills, milestone stories or meeting notes.
changes.now: Your assistant can suggest workstream descriptions, the planning guide, skills and needs, milestone stories, gate descriptions and meeting notes, and change a workstream's color, dates and order. Deleting a workstream always waits for you, and only works on an empty one. Review shows the text as it is now and as it would be.

changes.title: Your assistant sees what's missing
changes.now: What your assistant reads now includes skills, needs, milestone stories, gate descriptions and Jira descriptions, and lists exactly which workstreams, people, work and milestones are still missing a description, skills or needs. The planning guide preview shows the same list.

changes.title: Moves from the assistant
changes.before: An assistant's move of an initiative or milestone could be refused as changed since, even when nothing had changed.
changes.now: Moves written from what the assistant reads apply, including for initiatives that start and milestones that fall partway through a week.

changes.title: Older copies open these plans read-only
changes.now: A plan with skills, assistant notes, milestone stories or gate descriptions opens read-only in older copies of Sightline, so they can't drop them. Update every copy your team uses to keep editing.

headline: A menu down the left side

changes.title: Every page has one home
changes.before: Pages were split between tabs, a More menu and Settings, and Sort Jira work opened from Settings but showed up under Work.
changes.now: A menu on the left lists Work, Delivery, Product updates and Settings with every page under its group. Sort Jira work and Jira change proposals live only in Work, and counts and warnings sit on the page they belong to.

changes.title: Fold the menu to a rail
changes.now: Collapse the menu to a narrow rail of icons with the button at its top or the \ key, and hover or focus an icon to open its group. Sightline remembers your choice in this browser, and narrow windows start with the rail.

changes.title: Settings key and Jira hints
changes.before: Pressing 4 didn't open Settings, and some messages sent you to Settings to sort Jira work.
changes.now: Pressing 4 opens Settings, and messages point to Work, then Sort Jira work, or to Settings, then Jira connection.

headline: Workstream names stay in view

changes.title: Workstream names stay in view as you scroll
changes.before: Scrolling down a long workstream, especially in Days, moved its name off the screen, so you lost track of which workstream you were in.
changes.now: Each workstream's name stays just under the dates while its rows are on screen. In Days the next workstream's header slides over it as you reach it; in Weeks the name moves down with its row. It also stays below any rows you've pinned with Show, then While scrolling. Printing is unchanged.

headline: A calmer planning assistant panel

changes.title: The conversation comes first
changes.before: The panel stacked the connection, the message box, setup steps, privacy notes, skills and files at the same weight, with two lines saying the folder was connected.
changes.now: One line at the top says whether your assistant is connected, with a dot that pulses while a reply is on its way. Your messages and the assistant's read as a conversation, an empty one offers two ways to start, and the message box shows what you're asking about.

changes.title: Setup and files, out of the way
changes.before: Opening a setup section ran its text into the next one.
changes.now: Connection steps, what's kept where, planning skills and the assistant's files are quiet rows under Setup and files at the end of the panel. An open row is set apart, and the commands sit in their own box.
changes.where: Planning assistant panel, Setup and files

changes.title: You can tell what to click
changes.before: Some actions were buttons and others underlined text, and the older-tools warning was one long sentence of file names.
changes.now: Every action in the panel is a button: Refresh, Export, Disconnect, Skip and Edit included. Pause and when changes apply sit together in one box, and the older-tools warning names the version once, shows the files as chips and offers Replace or Keep.

headline: Edit your assistant's milestone moves

changes.title: Edit shows a change's fields
changes.before: Edit on a change that moves a milestone, or on most other changes, opened an empty box.
changes.now: Edit shows the change's own fields, such as a milestone move's date and whether it's the stretch date, and checks your edit the same way as the assistant's version. A change with nothing you can edit says so: skip it and ask your assistant.

changes.title: Milestone moves read plainly
changes.before: A change that cleared a stretch date read "move true → null".
changes.now: It reads "stretch date cleared", and a move reads as a move to a date.

headline: Your assistant proposes where Jira work goes

changes.title: The assistant proposes where unsorted Jira work belongs
changes.before: Your assistant could read Jira issues but couldn't tell which ones were waiting in Sort Jira work, and couldn't propose placing them.
changes.now: Your assistant reads what's waiting in Sort Jira work against each workstream's planning guide and the initiatives already there, and proposes a place for each issue: a workstream, an initiative, or not ours. An epic's stories that belong together move together. Every placement waits for you to review it, at every assistant level, and nothing is written to Jira.

changes.title: Review Jira placements in one table
changes.now: Placements show as one table with the issue, where it goes, the assistant's reason, and high or low confidence. Edit offers only the places the issue can go. Skip leaves it in Sort Jira work. Apply ready applies up to 25 as one update, with one Undo.

changes.title: A Sort Jira work skill
changes.now: The bundled planning skills include Sort Jira work: it groups issues by epic, proposes placements with reasons, sends them for review, and reports what was placed, skipped, changed since, and what it couldn't place, with the question it would need answered.

changes.title: Bring back issues marked not ours
changes.before: An issue in a sprint marked not ours stayed hidden from Sort Jira work unless you undid it right away.
changes.now: Sort Jira work says how many issues are marked not ours, and Show them again brings them back.

changes.title: The helper accepts --json where the guide puts it
changes.before: sightline-app.py refused --json written after the command, as the guide and skills write it.
changes.now: It accepts --json before or after the command.

headline: Every button answers when you hover and click

changes.title: Controls answer your hover and click
changes.before: Many buttons and chips didn't change when you pointed at them, nothing moved when you clicked, and a selected button could show a gray ring or light, clipped corners.
changes.now: Every button, chip, tab, menu item and row lightens when you point at it and presses in when you click. Filled buttons keep their color on hover, and the keyboard focus ring stays visible everywhere.

changes.title: Switches slide to what you pick
changes.before: Choices like the source and layout switches swapped a dark fill from one option to the next.
changes.now: The selected option is a raised pill that slides to the one you pick. The main navigation underlines the view you're on.

changes.title: Bars glide to their new dates
changes.now: When an edit, undo or redo moves a few bars, they glide from where they were and glow once, so you can see what changed. A new view or a drag doesn't animate, and nothing moves if your system asks for reduced motion.

changes.title: A new typeface, built into the page
changes.before: The page loaded its font from the internet, so it looked different offline.
changes.now: Sightline uses Instrument Sans, with narrower headings and bar labels so more of a name fits. The font is part of the file, so it looks the same offline and the page makes no network requests.

changes.title: Long links in Breakdown read left to right
changes.before: A link that wrapped onto two lines in an initiative's Breakdown was centered.
changes.now: It lines up on the left like the text around it.

changes.title: Similar sprint names no longer look the same
changes.before: In Settings, long sprint names were cut off at the end, so names like "Platform Sprint 15" and "Platform Sprint 16" read the same.
