changes.now: The name column has room for typical sprint names. Where a name still has to be cut, the timeline header and the commitment table cut it in the middle and keep the end, such as S15, in view. Point at a name to see all of it.
changes.where: Settings, Timeboxes and ceremonies; Timeline header

changes.title: A short count on the Settings tab
changes.before: The Settings tab showed a sentence such as "87 stories in a sprint" in a red pill, with the warning sign pressed against the word.
changes.now: It shows just the number. Point at it to read what it counts; screen readers still hear the full words. The warning sign has its own space.

headline: The assistant keeps your timeboxes in line with the work

changes.title: The assistant can set timebox goals and names
changes.before: No assistant change could touch a sprint, so goals had to be typed in by hand after a plan cleanup.
changes.now: The assistant can set the name and goal of the plan's own timeboxes, add one at the end, or add timeboxes through a date, the same way Add timeboxes through does: at most 60 at a time, and asking again once they reach the date changes nothing. Several goals in one change apply as one update with one undo.

changes.title: The context lists your timeboxes and what finishes in each
changes.now: The context file lists the plan's timeboxes in order: Jira sprints, the rows between them and the plan's own, with the plan's dates, Jira's own dates, the goal, and the tasks, initiatives and milestones finishing in each. The guide says to write a goal as one plain line about what that timebox finishes.
changes.where: Assistant panel, Files and assistant handoff

changes.title: Jira sprints stay where Jira puts them
changes.before: A Jira sprint's name and goal were read-only, but its length could change and rows could be moved or deleted around it, which moved its dates.
changes.now: A Jira sprint can't be lengthened, moved or deleted here, and neither can a row whose change would move one, such as the weeks between two Jira sprints. Those rows' goals are still yours. Each locked control says why, and the assistant is refused the same way: This sprint comes from Jira; change it in Jira.

headline: Assistant batches apply in order, and the right tools are one click away

changes.title: Changes that build on each other are ready together
changes.before: A change that used a task an earlier change in the same batch adds showed red until the earlier one was applied.
changes.now: The panel checks a batch in order. A change an earlier one enables shows Ready after change N, with that change's summary. Skip a change and the ones it enables say they need it, with Reopen.

changes.title: Apply ready applies in order and says what happened
changes.before: Apply ready left out changes that depended on others, and it was hard to tell what had landed.
changes.now: Apply ready applies the ready changes from the top as one update with one undo, and stops at the first one that can't apply. It then says which changes applied, which were already in the plan, which was skipped, what waits and why, and whether the plan was saved.

changes.title: Put assistant tools in this folder
changes.now: One click puts the assistant tools that match this page in the assistant folder, each with a .sha256 checksum. Files it doesn't recognize are never replaced, and it asks before replacing an older copy. The context file says whether the folder's tools match.
changes.where: Assistant panel, Files and assistant handoff

changes.title: Held changes hold what they enable
changes.now: When a change waits for review, is paused, has expired or was written against an older plan, the changes it enables wait with it and say why. Size and delete checks look at the plan as the earlier changes leave it.
changes.where: Assistant panel, When your assistant writes changes

changes.title: Results right after an apply while editing
changes.before: After applying a change while editing, the results file still said it was waiting and the change it enabled was invalid.
changes.now: The results file describes the plan as it is in this browser, says when it isn't saved yet, and carries the same summary the page shows.

changes.title: Moving a milestone with its date as prev
changes.before: An assistant moving a milestone with prev given as a date was told the milestone had changed since.
changes.now: prev is a date, as the context gives it, and a stretch date can now be cleared (stretch true, day null).

changes.title: The checking tool says what it checked
changes.now: check-amendments checks a batch in order, and lists what it checked and what only Sightline checks when it applies the batch.

changes.title: Start-up help for synced folders
changes.now: If Sightline doesn't start, the first step it suggests is to wait for OneDrive or another synced folder to finish syncing, then reload.

headline: Stories: the why behind each item

changes.title: Write a story for any initiative or task
changes.now: Each initiative and task can have a story: why it exists, what it delivers and when it's done. Edit shows a live preview beside the text, and a new story starts from a template.
changes.where: Click an item, then Write a story or Edit

changes.title: See the story at a glance
changes.now: Hovering an item shows the first lines of its story, or No story yet. Click it to read the whole story in its details.

changes.title: Walk an initiative's breakdown
changes.now: An initiative's details list its tasks with their owner, status and whether each has a story. Click one to open it, and Up and Down move to the next item while the details are open.

changes.title: Jira descriptions as stories
changes.now: An item linked to Jira shows the issue's description, marked From Jira. What the plan had before is kept as a draft, and is shown when Jira's description is empty. Run the updated sync to bring descriptions in.

changes.title: Story templates
changes.now: Set the starting text for new initiative and task stories, for the whole plan.

changes.title: Assistants can read and propose stories
changes.now: The assistant context includes stories and templates, and an assistant can propose stories for many items at once. Review shows each story in full and Edit opens it in a text box. A batch applies as one update with one undo. Older copies of Sightline open a plan with stories read-only.

headline: Hide what you don't need, and pin the top rows

changes.title: Show: hide gates, meetings, done work and more
changes.now: Show has an eye for each kind of item: gates, releases, deliverables, meetings, process blocks, milestones and done work. One click hides or shows a kind on Timeline, List and People. Focus hides meetings, process blocks and done work at once.

changes.title: Pin the top rows while you scroll
changes.before: The Gates, Releases, Deliverables, Team meetings and Process rows scrolled away with the workstreams.
changes.now: Pin the top rows keeps them under the dates while you scroll, so you can see what's coming next to any workstream.

changes.title: Keys to clear the chart
changes.now: G hides or shows gates, M hides or shows meetings, H opens Show, and Shift+H shows everything you hid. In any meeting, gate, process block, release or milestone, Hide all hides that kind.
changes.where: Timeline, List and People, and an item's details

changes.title: Kinds can be hidden, not only shown
changes.before: Kind chips in Filters could only show one kind and leave out the rest.
changes.now: Each kind cycles through Show only, Hide and off, and Hide wins. Releases, deliverables and done work can be hidden too. The line under the toolbar says what's hidden, with Show everything.

changes.title: Saved views remember what's hidden
changes.now: What you hide stays in this browser for each plan, and a saved view keeps its own choice. A plan whose team views hide kinds opens read-only in older copies of Sightline, so they can't drop the setting.

headline: Read the whole plan as a list

changes.title: A List page next to Timeline
changes.now: List shows the same work Timeline draws, as rows: Start, End, Item, Owner, Waits on and Status. Read it by initiative, by person, or as one list by start date. Work Timeline doesn't draw is at the end under Not on the timeline, with the reason.

changes.title: See what each item waits on
changes.now: Waits on names the task, initiative, gate or process step an item waits for, and links Jira dependencies to Jira, warning when one ends after the item starts. Click a name to open it.

changes.title: Copy or print the list
changes.now: Copy as table copies the rows as shown as a markdown table, ready to paste into a document. Print prints every row, with the header repeated on each page.
changes.where: List, Copy as table and Print

changes.title: Views and selection carry across
changes.now: A saved view applied on List stays on List. The selected item stays selected when you switch between Timeline and List, and a link to List opens the same layout and item.

headline: The whole forecast in one place

changes.title: A Forecast section in Capacity
changes.now: Capacity opens with the forecast for the whole plan: one line with how many items, their effort and the likely and high finish, then every initiative with its effort, start, likely and high finish, and why it starts when it does. Click an initiative to open it on the timeline.

changes.title: See when the forecast isn't complete
changes.now: When any initiative has no forecast date (no effort, nobody to do it, or waiting on something with no date), the summary says the forecast is incomplete, counts why, and doesn't claim a finish date for everything.

changes.title: The chain behind the last finish, and load by workstream
changes.now: Under the table: the critical chain that sets the last finish date, the workstream the waiting was for, and each workstream's demand against its people's time, with a weekly chart of Jira-dated work, forecast work and ready work waiting.

changes.title: Overlapping waits are counted once
changes.now: When naming the workstream most of the waiting was for, a working day that several steps of the chain spent waiting counts once.
changes.before: Overlapping waits were added together, so the count could be longer than the whole forecast.

changes.title: Clearer reasons
changes.now: Reasons read as plain sentences: "It starts then because it waited for Index rebuild (finishes Mar 20)."
changes.before: "It starts then because waited for Index rebuild."

headline: People rows draw their work again, and the assistant scripts travel with the page

changes.title: Rows by person show their work
changes.now: With rows by person, in Weeks and in Days, each person's row draws their initiatives and tasks again.
changes.before: Every person row was empty, though its label counted the work: a style from the Jira proposals list squeezed the row's timeline to no width.

changes.title: The assistant scripts are published with the page
changes.now: Publishing the page also copies sightline-app.py and sightline-jira-sync.py beside it, each with a checksum file. Each copy says which Sightline version it matches (--version), and refuses, with the reason, to send or check against a page of another version, so an assistant on another computer can't check a batch against old actions.

changes.title: Clearer instructions for assistants
changes.now: The instructions an assistant reads now say, near the top, to take each action's arguments exactly as listed and never guess field names, and to check a batch with sightline-app.py check before handing it over.

headline: Why an initiative finishes when it does, and who the work waits for

changes.title: Follow the chain that sets a finish date
changes.now: An initiative's card has a "Why it finishes then" list. It walks back through what held the initiative up: the work it waited for, and the work that had or shared its people, each with dates, until it reaches the first day, a gate, a Jira sprint or a workstream's start.
changes.where: Initiative card, under the forecast dates (open "Why it finishes then")

changes.title: See which workstream the work is waiting for
changes.now: Under the chain, the card names the workstream, and its people, that most of the waiting was for, with the number of working days. When nobody on the chain waited for people, it names the busiest workstream instead: how much work it had against how much time its people had, and over which dates.
changes.where: Initiative card, at the end of "Why it finishes then"

changes.title: Waits are dated by working days
changes.now: When an initiative waited for its people, the dates given for the wait start and end on working days, not on a weekend or holiday.
changes.before: A wait could be dated from a Saturday when the forecast was worked out on a weekend.

headline: A forecast date on every initiative, with the reason for it

changes.title: See when an initiative is likely to finish
changes.now: An initiative with an effort shows its forecast on its card: the likely start and finish, and the finish if everything takes its high estimate. Sightline works it out day by day from who's in each workstream, their time, holidays and time off, what each item waits for, and the other work competing for the same people. It never moves anything on the timeline.
changes.where: The initiative card, under Effort left

changes.title: Know why a date is what it is
changes.now: The forecast says what set an item's start: the item it waited for, a gate, a Jira issue's sprint, or the work its people were on, with dates. It also gives the pace in person-weeks a week and who's on it.

changes.title: No date, with the reason, when the forecast can't give one
changes.now: An item gets no date, never a guess, when it waits for something with no effort, sits on a dependency loop, is in a workstream with nobody in it, or waits for a Jira issue with no sprint. The card says which one, and anything waiting on it says so too.

changes.title: Holders show their latest finish
changes.now: An initiative with others inside shows the forecast finish of the last of them, or how many have no date yet.
changes.where: The card of an initiative with others inside

headline: Capacity day by day, the second step toward a forecast

changes.title: Say when people join and leave
changes.now: A person's card has Joins on and Leaves on. Their capacity counts only the days in between, so someone starting mid-sprint or rolling off is planned for the days they're actually here.

changes.title: Split someone's time across workstreams
changes.now: For someone in two or more workstreams, the person card has Time split: a weight for each workstream. With no split, their time divides evenly. When a workstream ends, its share moves to their other workstreams.

changes.title: Keep time back for support and unplanned work
changes.now: Set a reserve for the team in Team, and a different one for any workstream on its card. The workstream card shows this week's capacity for planned work, in person-weeks, after the reserve.

changes.title: Sprint capacity counts joining and leaving dates
changes.now: A person's capacity for a sprint leaves out the days before they join and from the day they leave.
changes.before: Capacity counted every working day of the sprint, whatever their start or end date.

changes.title: Your assistant can set capacity inputs
changes.now: Assistant changes can set when someone joins or leaves, how their time splits across workstreams, and the team's or a workstream's reserve.

changes.title: Older copies open a plan with these settings read-only
changes.now: A plan with join or leave dates, time splits or reserves opens read-only in copies older than 1.103.0, so they can't save over them.
changes.where: Opening a plan in an older copy

headline: Effort estimates, the first step toward a forecast

changes.title: Give an initiative its effort left, in person-weeks
changes.now: Each initiative's card has Effort left (person-weeks): a likely figure, and a low and high if you know them. The card says what the forecast will do with it: Forecast, Fixed (Jira's sprint sets its dates), Not counted (no effort yet, which is never treated as zero), or Out of scope if you tick Leave out of the forecast. An initiative with others inside shows their sum.

changes.title: Link work to what it ships
changes.now: Delivers on an initiative's card links it to deliverables, and each deliverable's card lists what delivers it, or says Not forecast when nothing does. Linking the existing work, instead of adding a second initiative for it, keeps the same work from being counted twice.
changes.where: Initiative card, Delivers; deliverable card, Delivered by

changes.title: Your assistant can set effort and links
changes.now: Assistant changes can set an initiative's effort, leave it out of the forecast, and link it to what it delivers. It's told never to guess an effort.

changes.title: Older copies open a plan with effort read-only
changes.now: A plan with effort, scope or delivers opens read-only in copies older than 1.102.0, so they can't save over them.
changes.where: Opening a plan in an older copy

headline: Pause your assistant, and big changes wait for you

changes.title: Pause and Resume
changes.now: One click stops anything your assistant writes from applying on its own, whatever level you picked, until you click Resume. You can still review and apply changes by hand, and your assistant is told it's paused.

changes.title: Changes that move a lot wait for your review
changes.now: When your assistant's changes apply routine changes on their own, a change that would move more than 5 other items, or a batch touching more than 50 items, waits for you instead, and says why. At Apply everything, they apply as before.
changes.before: Any routine change applied on its own, however much of the plan it moved.
changes.where: Assistant panel, When your assistant writes changes

headline: See what your assistant changed, and undo a whole batch

changes.title: Items show when your assistant added or edited them
changes.now: Anything your assistant adds or changes is stamped with who it acted for and which assistant and batch did it, for example "edited by Avery via Planning bot". The stamp is kept when the plan is saved, reopened, merged or saved as YAML.
changes.before: Changes your assistant applied looked like you had made them by hand.
changes.where: The item card, under its title; Activity

changes.title: Undo this batch
changes.now: The Assistant panel lists the last five batches your assistant applied to the shared file, each with Undo this batch. Undo puts back only what that batch changed, even if other updates came after it, and leaves anything a teammate has changed since. It's available in this browser until you reload.
changes.where: Assistant panel, Applied by your assistant

changes.title: Older copies open a plan with assistant stamps read-only
changes.now: A plan with these stamps opens read-only in copies of Sightline older than 1.100.0, so they can't save over them. Update everyone's copy to keep editing together.
changes.where: Opening a plan in an older copy

headline: The header holds still while Sightline checks the file

changes.title: The page no longer bounces every 15 seconds
changes.now: The automatic check of the shared file (Check automatically) runs without touching the header or the editing bar, unless a save or check takes a while. The status line at the top says only what matters: who's editing, the last save and the lock.
changes.before: Each automatic check flashed "working…" and rewrote the status line at the top, which wrapped onto several lines and then shrank back, so the whole page jumped.
changes.where: The status line at the top, and the editing bar

headline: Your assistant can add holidays, and check its work before sending

changes.title: Assistant changes can add and remove holidays
changes.now: An assistant can add a day off for everyone, add a range such as a winter shutdown (stored as its working days, like the Holidays table does), or remove a holiday. The review shows what each one moves.
changes.before: Holidays had to be added by hand in Settings, Calendar.

changes.title: The assistant helper checks a batch before it sends it
changes.now: sightline-app.py check reads the batch against the context your assistant read, with no page open, and names each problem: an unknown action, a missing or extra argument, a bad date, a new item with no id, or a batch written against an older plan. send and run make the same check and send nothing if it fails.

headline: Assistant changes can apply on their own

changes.title: Choose whether your assistant's changes wait for you
changes.now: Pick a level for each plan: wait for your review, apply routine changes on their own, or apply everything. Deletes wait for you unless you choose everything, and deleting an initiative with Jira-linked work always waits. Each batch that applies is one quick update you can Undo.
changes.before: Every change your assistant wrote waited for you to click Apply.
changes.where: Assistant panel, When your assistant writes changes

changes.title: A change that can't apply says why instead of waiting quietly
changes.now: A batch written against an older version of the plan, one more than an hour old, or one that arrives while you have unsaved edits isn't applied on its own, and your assistant is told why. While the page is open, even in a background tab, it tells your assistant every 30 seconds that it's there, so the assistant knows when nobody's listening.
changes.where: Assistant panel; the results and status files in your private folder

changes.title: Meeting notes skill records decisions, risks and links
changes.now: The meeting-to-plan skill now records agreed decisions, risks, starts-after links and milestones as changes, instead of listing them for you to enter by hand.

headline: The timeline stays where you scrolled

changes.title: The timeline no longer jumps back to the top
changes.now: When the chart redraws, for example after a Jira sync, an assistant update, a teammate's save, or when you click Start editing or Done editing, the timeline stays on the rows you were looking at.
changes.before: Every redraw scrolled the timeline and the page back to the top, which looked like a jitter every minute or so.
changes.where: Timeline, in both Weeks and Days

headline: Your assistant can do the whole replan

changes.title: Assistant changes cover links, people, milestones, gates, risks and decisions
changes.now: An assistant's changes can now add and remove starts-after links, delete initiatives, add and rename workstreams, set people's roles, allocation and workstream, add milestones with what they're done after, add gates, and add or update risks and decisions. You review them together and apply them with one click.
changes.before: Assistants could only change deliverables, initiatives' and tasks' basic fields, and Jira proposals. Everything else had to be done by hand.

changes.title: Assistant changes say what they move and refuse what the chart would refuse
changes.now: Before you apply, each change lists every item it moves, with both dates and how much later. A link that would make a loop, a link inside one initiative, dates Jira sets, and work landing in blacked-out time are refused with the reason, the same as when you edit by hand.

headline: Dragging on the chart follows the same rules as editing

changes.title: Dragged items are stamped and kept out of blacked-out time
changes.now: When you drag an initiative, task or milestone on the chart, the change records who made it and when, like any other edit, and a drag that would land outside its workstream's dates is refused with the reason.
changes.before: A drag didn't record who changed the item, and could leave it in time its workstream had blacked out.
changes.where: Timeline, dragging initiatives, tasks and milestones

headline: Give your external assistant the planning picture

changes.title: Plan with capacity, dependencies, risks and decisions
changes.now: Your assistant context includes people, allocation and availability, workstream membership, dependencies, gates, milestones, risks and decisions. It calculates capacity and known Jira demand across the loaded active and future sprints. Parked work stays visible, and exact coverage counts explain any data omitted to fit the export. Notes and time-off descriptions stay excluded.
changes.before: Assistant context focused on roadmap edits, omitted capacity and decision data, and capped initiative and task lists without complete coverage counts.
changes.where: The private assistant folder and manual assistant context export

headline: Take your planning skills straight from the app

changes.title: Deploy planning skills directly from the HTML app
changes.now: The HTML includes the planning skills from its build. Download them as a ZIP or install them into a chosen folder from the Planning assistant or Planning guide, without source code, npm or Python. Existing different files are kept, and the bundle shows its Sightline version.
changes.where: Planning assistant → Planning skills; Settings → Planning guide → Get planning skills

headline: Get clearer, more reliable assistant guidance

changes.title: Match proposal results and explain the source of a plan summary
changes.now: The six external assistant skills check plan and proposal identities before reporting outcomes. Status summaries distinguish saved shared snapshots from browser state and manual exports. Pending proposals allow read-only reviews and guide drafts to continue, and guide text is grouped by the fields in Settings.
changes.before: Matching revision numbers and Jira timestamps could be mistaken for matching proposal batches, and manual exports could be described as saved.
changes.where: The six planning skills installed with the sightline command

headline: Take your plan from first idea to team conversation

changes.title: Install the app and six reusable planning skills
changes.now: The public npm package installs the self-contained HTML app and six assistant skills. A visual walkthrough covers first use, four-quarter planning, Jira context, and reviewing AI proposals. Existing different files are kept; install into a new folder to update.

changes.title: Start with clear, invented planning examples
changes.now: The idea composer uses a general onboarding example. The public guide includes an invented team plan, Jira snapshot and two prepared proposals so you can try the review loop without an AI account.

headline: Keep context when following up with your assistant

changes.title: Retain the selected outcome or quarters in conversation history
changes.now: Follow-up requests retain the stable outcome IDs or quarters that belonged to earlier questions, including when you switch outcomes. Historical selections are labeled as earlier context. Requests keep complete recent turns within the existing message limit and preserve the full question length.
changes.before: The visible conversation showed earlier selections, but only the latest selection reached the assistant, making cross-outcome follow-ups ambiguous.

changes.title: Reconnect the changes file or folder you already selected
changes.now: Reconnect in the Planning assistant requests access to the existing individual changes file or private assistant folder. Paused file connections are labeled as files.
changes.before: The top Reconnect button took individual-file users into folder setup instead of reconnecting their existing changes file.

headline: Describe a plan change in one message

changes.title: Start with your notes and see what the assistant is working on
changes.now: Plan with AI opens an empty composer with the selected quarters in Working on. Ask assistant about this selects an outcome by its stable ID. Paste notes or describe a change and Send once; the selection travels with the request. The composer comes first, with setup and file details below.
changes.where: Product updates → Roadmap → Plan with AI, or open an outcome → Ask assistant about this.

changes.title: Keep roadmap ideas when opening your assistant
changes.now: Unsubmitted roadmap ideas stay with their plan during navigation and redraws in this tab's session. A successful submission clears only the text that was submitted. Untouched assistant starters follow a new selection; a question you have written keeps its original context until you choose Switch context.
changes.before: Opening Plan with AI cleared a new roadmap idea. An untouched generated assistant question could also keep pointing at an earlier outcome.

headline: Plan four quarters with your assistant

changes.title: Focus on four quarters and ask about an outcome
changes.now: Choose a starting calendar quarter for a four-quarter roadmap, or switch to Long range. Work outside the window stays counted and recoverable. Plan with AI prepares a question using the displayed quarters; each outcome has Ask assistant about this. Questions keep existing drafts and wait for Send.
changes.where: Product updates → Roadmap. Horizon choices stay in this browser; plan contents are unchanged.

changes.title: Check for a reply before your first planning conversation
changes.now: Test reply sends a short question with the saved plan context through your configured companion and preserves your unfinished message. A matching response confirms a reply for that snapshot; test responses cannot introduce proposed changes. Starter questions help organize roadmap notes or review gaps.
changes.where: Connect assistant → Test reply, with the local companion configured and running.

changes.title: See the welcome screen and know what Today can assess
changes.now: A fresh browser renders the welcome screen immediately. Today offers a planning step when no work is loaded, explains when Jira data is needed, and qualifies quiet summaries when connected data is stale or incomplete.
changes.before: A fresh browser could show a blank Timeline until navigation. Today could declare all clear before work or Jira status data was loaded.

headline: Talk through changes to your plan

changes.title: Turn a planning conversation into reviewed changes
changes.now: Ask questions, capture ideas, and refine proposed changes in the assistant panel. An optional local companion connects to your company's Chat Completions endpoint using a separate private configuration file. Replies use the saved plan and Planning guide; proposed changes wait for review and Apply, with normal undo and shared Save controls.
changes.where: Connect assistant → conversation, with the local companion running against the same private assistant folder.

headline: Project guidance for your assistant

changes.title: Explain how your project is organized
changes.now: Settings → Planning guide lets the team describe project scope, workstream purposes, work breakdown, vocabulary, planning rules, and examples. Save it with the plan to include it in assistant context, or preview and copy the instructions. Guide drafts wait for an explicit Save guide; older app copies open plans with saved guidance read-only.
changes.where: Settings → Planning guide, or Planning guide in the assistant panel.

headline: A clearer way to open Sightline

changes.title: Find the ready-to-use app
changes.now: The repository start page links to the built app and explains how to open your separate plan file. If you open the development template, a notice points to the app in a new tab while keeping your current work available.

changes.title: See which version is open
changes.now: The current app version appears beside What's new without opening a dialog. The development template identifies itself and directs you to the built app instead of opening an empty release history.

headline: Safer reconnects and more reliable Find

changes.title: Keep edits with their original plan
changes.now: When you have browser edits, reconnecting stops if the file now contains a different plan. Your edits stay intact so you can download them before opening another plan.

changes.title: Reveal milestones hidden by a people filter
changes.now: Finding a milestone clears a people filter when it would keep the milestone hidden. Restore previous view brings back your original filter.

headline: Safer updates and easier daily work

changes.title: Keep unsaved work during lock and reconnect problems
changes.now: A teammate's active edit lock leaves your plan, undo history and recovery draft intact. Reconnecting compares the saved file with your original version and preserves your current edits before merging or asking you to resolve a conflict.

changes.title: Keep the message you are writing
changes.now: Refreshing Jira or redrawing details keeps unsent notes, quick updates and blocker explanations for each item in this session, including your cursor position. Submitting clears only the message that was sent.

changes.title: Reach routine work directly
changes.now: Sort Jira work is available under Work. Choose yourself in the toolbar to use Mine and author your updates. Find reveals matching milestones, gates and notes even when filters or layers hide them, with an option to restore your previous view.

changes.title: See feedback and keep your place
changes.now: Status messages remain visible on narrower screens. Filters retain keyboard focus after updating, and Today names the person who decides each due decision, including when no decider is set.

changes.title: Refresh the screen you are using
changes.now: Other workspaces leave the hidden Timeline and setup tables alone. Text edits update the plan immediately and combine derived screen updates while you type; returning to a workspace renders current data.

changes.title: Refuse oversized updates without changing the plan
changes.now: Deliverable limits are checked on a private candidate before an update reaches the live plan. Repeated initiative and task additions with the same details stay completed, including changes that add an item and then set its fields.

changes.title: Count unfinished board work consistently
changes.now: Sprint history follows the board's final column when determining completed work, matching the page. An issue in a non-final review column stays unfinished even if Jira categorizes its status as done. Earlier recorded days are retained.

headline: Clearer shared-file refresh and recovery

changes.title: Check for teammates' updates automatically
changes.now: Shared plans check the local file every 15 seconds by default. An explicit choice to turn checks off is remembered. Automatic checks wait while you type, drag or use a dialog.

changes.title: Know what saved means
changes.now: Shared-file status distinguishes a local save from OneDrive synchronization and shows when the local file was last checked. Check OneDrive itself to confirm cloud synchronization.

changes.title: Review another copy before recovering work
changes.now: Compare a recovery copy with the current shared file and download backups. Choose deliberately whether to bring that copy into the editor, then review it before saving.

headline: Clearer workspaces and a connected assistant

changes.title: Work, Delivery and Product updates
changes.now: Find Today and Sprint under Work; Timeline, Capacity, Status update, Decisions and Risks under Delivery; Roadmap and release notes under Product updates. Settings holds the team, calendar and Jira connection. Each group remembers where you were.

changes.title: Saved views remember which sources you chose
changes.now: Personal and team views now save and restore All sources, Jira only or Jira + mine. Changing sources marks the view modified, and All work restores all sources.

changes.title: Controls match the view you are using
changes.now: View and filter controls appear on Timeline and Capacity, where they apply. Roadmap and Status update clearly describe the whole plan. Your Timeline filters stay ready for when you return.

changes.title: Connect your assistant once
changes.now: Choose a private folder. Sightline keeps context and results current; your assistant writes proposed changes for you to review. Shared context comes from the confirmed saved file. Reconnect when browser permission expires.
changes.where: Connect assistant in the toolbar; Edge or Chrome.

changes.title: Common actions first
changes.now: Initiative and task details keep routine updates visible and put organizing or moving the item behind a disclosure. Deliverable timing explains its source and separates target windows from commitments.

changes.title: Refresh only what changed for the assistant
changes.now: Changing views leaves unchanged assistant context alone. Export lookups are indexed, and navigation uses cached controls so it stays cheap as more screens are opened.

headline: Rows by epic follow every parent link

changes.title: Rows by epic go past the epic
changes.now: Rows by epic now nest by any parent link, not only epics: an epic under its feature, the feature under its initiative, as deep as Jira goes. Each row says what it is (Feature, Initiative), and a task linked to a sub-task sits on its story's epic.

changes.title: The sync brings the parents above your epics
changes.now: The Jira helper now also fetches the parents above what it syncs (Parent Link or parent), up to six levels, and writes them apart from your issues, so they never show up as work to sort. Copy the new sightline-jira-sync.py next to the plan.

headline: Rows by epic in the Days view

changes.title: By epic in Days too
changes.now: The Days view now has rows by epic as well: the same nesting, summary bars, and Expand all and Collapse all, with each story and task on its day. Still read-only, since the tree comes from Jira.

headline: Timeline rows by epic

changes.title: Rows by epic, nested
changes.now: By epic puts one row per Jira epic, nested the way Jira's parent links nest, each with a bar spanning everything under it. Top epics open one level down; expand or collapse any row, or all of them. Work not under an epic sits on No epic, and a parent the sync didn't bring is named. It comes from Jira, so nothing drags there.

headline: Jira stories by person, and keys that fit

changes.title: By person shows Jira stories
changes.now: Each Jira story now sits on its assignee's row, in Weeks and Days, and counts toward what they have active. Unassigned stories go on Unassigned. An initiative carried by its stories no longer also sits on Unassigned. A plan run from Jira used to show almost nothing by person.

changes.title: Jira keys no longer run into names
changes.now: When a task or story is too short for its name, its Jira key moves into the label to its right instead of being cut off inside the bar.

headline: Senior review 16: safer bulk sorting

changes.title: Bulk sort never counts stories nobody picked
changes.now: Sorting stories only groups them into their epic's initiative when the Jira files list all of that epic's stories, and only the ones on that list. Otherwise each story goes on by itself, so an initiative never counts stories you didn't pick. A parent that isn't an epic is no longer treated as one.

changes.title: Bulk sort respects what just changed
changes.now: Sorting a story from a parked epic brings the epic back with only that story. Every sort is decided again on the latest file, so a teammate's placement, epic link, parking or Not ours from a moment ago wins. Accept suggested is one save, so one Undo takes it all back, and number keys no longer also switch pages.

headline: Plan setup, and fewer tabs for readers

changes.title: Manage is now Plan setup, in four groups
changes.now: Manage is now Plan setup, and its 15 sections are grouped: Lists (Milestones, Gates, Decisions, Risks, Tags), Team (Team, Calendar, Meetings, Timeboxes & ceremonies), Jira (Sort Jira work, Proposals, Jira connection) and Reports (Status update, Snapshots, Activity). Jira work is now Sort Jira work, and Jira is Jira connection. Links to the old places still open.

changes.title: Fewer tabs while you're reading
changes.now: Someone only reading a shared plan sees Today, Timeline, Sprint and Roadmap, with People and Plan setup under More. Start editing and all six are back. The page you're on always keeps its tab.

headline: Today at a glance

changes.title: A summary at the top of Today
changes.now: Today now opens with a summary: what needs attention (to escalate, blocked, stale, late, should have started, decisions due; each jumps to its list), what's coming up (the next milestone and Jira release, and this quarter's deliverables with how many are at risk), and buttons to the Roadmap, Sprint and Timeline. The work queue follows below.

headline: A gentler first look

changes.title: Clear next steps on an empty plan
changes.now: Reconnecting a shared file is one clear button in the middle of the page. An empty shared plan you're reading says so and offers Start editing to set it up. An empty plan you're editing gets a short checklist (name it, name workstreams, add the first initiative, optionally bring in Jira and share it) that ticks itself off and goes away once there's work.
changes.where: Timeline, on an empty or reconnecting plan.

changes.title: Quieter setup notes for readers
changes.now: Someone only reading a shared plan sees setup offers (like switching to Jira's sprints) as one quiet line, "1 setup note for whoever runs this plan · Show". Blockers, like reconnecting the file or recovering unsaved edits, still show in full, and editors see everything.

headline: Start with your page

changes.title: Start with
changes.now: Choose the page Sightline opens on: Today, My work (Today, just yours), Timeline, Sprint, Team capacity or Roadmap, or where you left off. It's yours, in this browser; links and reloads still open where they point.

headline: What a story serves

changes.title: Serves on story cards
changes.now: A Sprint card now says which deliverable its story is for ("Serves Faster checkout"), when the deliverable links the story itself or its feature or epic, so developers see the customer-facing thing behind the work.

headline: Sort Jira work in bulk

changes.title: Sort Jira work into the plan, in bulk
changes.now: Jira work now offers Sort them in bulk: everything in a sprint or your searches that isn't on the plan, grouped by epic, sprint, assignee or label. Pick whole groups or Shift-click a range, then drop on a workstream, click it, press its number, or use Move to. Accept suggested sorts each group to where its people already have work.

changes.title: Stories from one epic become one initiative
changes.now: Stories you sort from the same epic become one initiative for that epic, with its other stories switched off, instead of one initiative per story: 70 stories under 10 epics are 10 initiatives. Dropping on an initiative adds them to it. Every drop is one save, with Undo.

headline: Smoother everyday use

changes.title: The status line reads properly
changes.now: The status line ran the file's state into the buttons' labels ("revision 73Start editingSave as you go"). It now shows just the state: "Read-only · Team.json · saved 3:02 PM · revision 73".
changes.where: The status line at the bottom.

changes.title: Before we commit: the sprint being planned, and a check before recording
changes.now: Before we commit opens on the next sprint in the week before it starts, otherwise on the one running now. Recording a commitment while things are still flagged asks first and names them, so you can add an assumption.

changes.title: What changed at a glance
changes.now: Today says how many things changed right under its heading, with a link to the list; past the first 12 plan changes, See all opens Activity. The time Jira is compared from is in the panel's header.

changes.title: Smaller touches
changes.now: Snapshot groups can show every item. The status update says when its draft was made. The Deliverables row keeps a Roadmap link when only broader ones exist, and reads out ship days. The amendment editor names items instead of ids. Amendments open faster: what a date change moves is only worked out while their panel is open.

headline: Senior review 15

changes.title: Safer handling of odd plan files
changes.now: A plan whose id is a reserved word gets a safe one, so it can't disturb the page's settings. If teammates' snapshots merge past the limit of 12, none are dropped (adding a new one still waits until there's room).

changes.title: Amendment edits you can trust
changes.now: Saving the editor no longer breaks an amendment that changes owners (owner lists aren't edited as text). If this browser can't store your edits, it says so and keeps the editor open instead of saying they were saved. Only recent batches' edits are kept.

changes.title: check-amendments refuses NaN
changes.now: The offline checker now refuses NaN and Infinity in an amendments file, as the page does, instead of calling it ready.

changes.title: Smaller fixes
changes.now: A plan title can't add headings to the Markdown copy of a status update. A deliverable whose release ships before its Jira work's sprints now starts at its ship day on the Timeline, so the ship mark sits on its bar.

headline: Amendments for initiatives and tasks

changes.title: Your assistant can amend initiatives and tasks
changes.now: Amendments can now add initiatives and tasks, and change their name, status, owners, workstream and dates. The review shows how many linked items a date change would move before you apply it. Jira-linked items keep Jira's status and dates (propose those in Jira instead), and dates that come from tasks can't be set directly.
changes.where: Roadmap, Assistant amendments; the sync's check-amendments checks them too.

headline: Check amendments offline

changes.title: check-amendments in the sync script
changes.now: The sync script can now check an amendments file against the plan without opening Sightline: python sightline-jira-sync.py check-amendments plan.json amendments.json. It uses the same rules as the page and lists each change as ready, changed since, invalid or already in the plan, with the reason; --json prints it for your assistant. The page still checks again when you apply.
changes.where: The sync script; the guide in Export for your assistant says to use it.

headline: Edit an amendment before applying it

changes.title: Edit your assistant's amendments
changes.now: Each waiting amendment now has Edit: fix a name, a target, the Jira keys or a proposal's value before you apply it. Your edits stay in this browser and are checked as strictly as the assistant's own; Apply writes the edited version. If your assistant rewrites that change, your edit stops applying and the change says so. Use the assistant's version puts it back.

headline: Deliverables in the Days view

changes.title: The Deliverables row in the Days view
changes.now: The Deliverables row now shows in the Days view too, from the first working day of its linked Jira work's sprints, with its ship day marked. Click one to open it.

headline: Before we commit

changes.title: A check before the sprint starts
changes.now: The Sprint tab opens with Before we commit for the sprint about to start: its goal, points against the team's capacity, and what to look at: not estimated, not assigned, people with work who are out, assignees not on the team, sprint work not on the plan, gates during the sprint, and work outside its workstream's dates.
changes.where: Sprint tab. Switch between this sprint and the next.

changes.title: Record sprint commitment
changes.now: Record what the team took on (issues, points, capacity, and any assumption) in the shared file. Afterwards the check shows what changed since: points added, removed and re-estimated.

headline: Risks and decisions that move

changes.title: Next action, waiting on, escalate by, who decides
changes.now: Decisions now have who decides, a next action, what they're waiting on and an escalate-by date; risks get the same, plus open or closed. The status update includes them.

changes.title: An Escalate list
changes.now: Today now opens with risks and decisions past their escalate-by date, and decisions past when they were needed: who decides, the next action, what it's waiting on, and how far over. Mine shows the ones you own or decide. The Today badge counts them.

headline: Status update

changes.title: Prepare a status update
changes.now: A draft status update from the plan: On track, Changed, At risk, Decisions needed and Next milestone, with a suggested overall status. Edit any part, copy it as text or Markdown, and save a frozen copy to the shared file. The next update's Changed compares with the last saved one (or the newest snapshot).

headline: Snapshots

changes.title: Snapshots to compare against
changes.now: Save a named snapshot of the plan ("Q4 commit") and compare today with it: what's later or earlier and by how many working days, what was added, removed or dropped, what finished, and which deliverables were retimed. Snapshots are in the shared file (up to 12), so everyone sees the same ones.

changes.title: Slip marks from any snapshot
changes.now: Show slip on the Timeline makes a snapshot the baseline, so the Timeline's slip marks and summary compare with it by name ("Since Q4 commit: 3 slipped"). Set baseline still works as before.

headline: What changed

changes.title: What changed since your last visit
changes.now: Today now opens with what changed: teammates' plan changes (yours are summed up) and Jira's (done, started, changed sprint, new, release dates moved). Choose your last visit, yesterday or this week. Jira is compared with a daily summary of earlier syncs that this browser keeps; nothing goes into the plan file.
changes.where: Today, top of the right column. Click a line to open it.

headline: Deliverables on the Timeline

changes.title: A Deliverables row
changes.now: Planned and done deliverables with a quarter, a date or a Jira release now show in a row under Releases. Each spans its linked Jira work's sprints and shows its progress; a release or date marks its ship day, and one with no sprint dates yet is a faint band across its quarter. Broader ones (a half, a year, Later) stay on the Roadmap and are counted in the row's header.
changes.where: Timeline, weeks view. Click one to open it.

headline: Jira's facts stay Jira's

changes.title: Saving no longer copies Jira's status and sprint dates into the plan
changes.now: A save used to write Jira's status and sprint dates into the plan file as if someone had edited them. They now stay on screen only: saves, drafts, backups, downloads and merges keep the plan's own values. Jira's facts are applied again on every draw, so when Jira stops covering an item, the plan's own values come back.

headline: Quick updates draw once

changes.title: One redraw per quick update
changes.now: A quick update used to redraw the page twice: once while it was applied and again once it was saved. It now redraws once, when the save is confirmed, including after a retry because a teammate saved at the same moment.

changes.title: A refused quick update no longer stays on screen
changes.now: When a quick update couldn't be saved (for example, it would push the plan over 2 MB), the page kept showing the change even though the file didn't have it. It now shows the file's version, with the reason in the status line.

headline: Undo that costs almost nothing

changes.title: Undo kept as change records
changes.now: Undo used to keep a full copy of the plan for every step; older steps are now kept as the few hundred bytes that undo them, so a long editing session uses a fraction of the memory. Each step is checked when it's stored; the rare one that can't be described that way keeps its copy, so undo and redo are always exact.

changes.title: Bigger changes stay undoable from Activity
changes.now: Activity's Undo this now works for changes up to 96 KB (it was 16 KB), which covers a large Apply of assistant amendments. Anything bigger is listed as too big to undo from there, instead of the undo quietly disappearing.

headline: How big is the plan?

changes.title: Plan size
changes.now: Manage, Activity now shows how big the plan file is against the 2 MB a save can write, and what takes the most room (the change log, initiatives, deliverables, notes). Past 1 MB it warns that saves slow down on a synced drive; near 2 MB, that saves will stop.

headline: Data checked

changes.title: Know the numbers are complete
changes.now: Today, Sprint, the Roadmap and release notes now show a Data checked line: when Jira last synced, issues found against each search's total, linked keys not found, pull requests read against the sprint's issues, and whether the two Jira files are from one sync. Green is complete; amber says what's partial; red means a late or held-back sync. Check opens Jira setup.
changes.where: Today, Sprint, Roadmap, a release's notes.

changes.title: Copied notes say when data was partial
changes.now: When the Jira data isn't complete, copied release notes end with the Data checked line, so whoever pastes them knows. When it is complete, the notes stay clean for customers.
changes.where: A release's notes: Copy as text or Markdown.

headline: Senior review 13: amendments you can rely on

changes.title: Amendments keep working
changes.now: An amendments file that hadn't changed stopped working after its next 30-second check; it now stays loaded. Clearing a date no longer fails, and a change applies on a copy first, so it never lands halfway. Reads don't overlap, a file that's too big is refused before it's read, and switching plans drops the other plan's file.

changes.title: Hostile input is refused
changes.now: Amendment files can't use names that would change how the page works (like __proto__), odd values are refused rather than coerced, and link limits are enforced. Invalid wins over changed since. An add for an existing item must match everything it sets. Receipts follow what a change says, so an undone or rewritten change shows as Ready again.

changes.title: One set of rules
changes.now: Amendments now follow the same rules as editing a card: a target makes an idea Planned, no timing makes it an idea again, a release sets the quarter, and new wording needs approving again. Jira proposals from amendments record Jira's current value and use sprint and assignee ids, so they don't look stale at once.

changes.title: Release notes and pull requests
changes.now: Approvals are protected from older copies (they open the plan read-only), approval needs customer wording, and Markdown notes keep names as text. Merged pull requests are those updated this sprint, and a sprint with none says so. The export leaves notes out, lists linked Jira work first and says what it left out, and is there before a file is connected.
changes.where: A release's card; Sprint; Assistant amendments.

headline: Amendments from your AI assistant

changes.title: Your assistant's changes, reviewed first
changes.now: Connect a personal amendments file that your AI assistant writes. The Roadmap shows how many are waiting, new ones as dashed Proposed cards, and a proposed mark on cards they'd change. Nothing touches the shared plan until you apply it.

changes.title: Ready, Changed since, Needs attention
changes.now: Each change is checked strictly and gets a result with a reason: Ready, Changed since (the plan moved after your assistant wrote it), Needs attention (something in it isn't allowed), or Completed. Apply one, or apply the ready ones as one quick update; each is checked again on the latest file as it saves, and Jira links merge by membership. Skip and Reopen are remembered.

changes.title: What your assistant reads
changes.now: Export for your assistant saves a view of this plan's deliverables, workstreams, people, releases and targets, with the rules for writing amendments, an example, and a note to treat all names and notes as data. Version 1 covers deliverables (add, change fields, link or unlink Jira work) and Jira change proposals.

headline: Customer release notes

changes.title: Release notes from your deliverables
changes.now: A Jira release's card now shows its release notes: its deliverables grouped by New, Improved and Fixed, each in its customer wording. Final lists only Done deliverables whose wording is approved; Draft shows everything planned, marked where it isn't done or approved. Copy as text or Markdown, or print just the notes.

changes.title: Approve the wording
changes.now: A Done deliverable with a release has Approve for release notes, which records who approved it and when. Changing its name, customer wording or kind clears the approval, so the notes always use approved words. Its badge says Approve for notes until then, then In release notes.

headline: Pull requests: what's done and what's left

changes.title: Active, Merged and Drafts
changes.now: Sprint's pull requests widget switches between Active (waiting for review: what's left), Merged this sprint (what's done), and Drafts. The sync now reads pull requests for the sprint's done issues too (reusing them for hours, since they rarely change), so merged ones show.

changes.title: A clearer idea form
changes.now: The Roadmap's quick add now labels its fields, New idea and From. From is optional, suggests your meetings, and remembers the last one you used in this plan; it no longer guesses today's meeting.

headline: Draft pull requests stay out of the way

changes.title: Only active pull requests
changes.now: Sprint's Open pull requests now lists active ones only; drafts (marked by Bitbucket, or titled Draft: or WIP) are hidden, with Show drafts to see them, marked Draft. Card PR counts and the PR waiting 3+ days filter leave drafts out too.

headline: Senior review 12: deliverables you can trust

changes.title: Linked Jira work is synced
changes.now: The sync now fetches Jira work linked to a deliverable even when it isn't on the board or in a search, so its progress and its epics' stories show.

changes.title: Honest progress
changes.now: A deliverable's progress uses the team's status mapping for epics too, says "about" (≈) when some stories are counted through their epic, and says how many linked issues weren't in the last sync, instead of showing 0/0.

changes.title: Split, delete and owners are safe to share
changes.now: Split builds its parts from the latest file and carries the release and date too; the original stays findable, lists its parts, and can move its Jira links to one. Delete stops if someone changed it since you opened it. Owners on a deliverable are a quick update, like its other fields.

changes.title: Limits refuse instead of dropping
changes.now: More deliverables or Jira links than a plan keeps are refused with a message, instead of vanishing on reload, and a plan with two deliverables sharing an id isn't opened. Chart drags' undo steps now stay within the undo memory budget.

changes.title: Smaller fixes
changes.now: Capacity says whose load is unknown (no Jira user) instead of counting them as within. An idea's From is remembered per plan. Many ideas get one When picker each. The Jira key box suggests as you type. A deliverable deleted elsewhere closes its panel. Timeboxes wording is consistent.

headline: Roadmap and deliverables

changes.title: A Roadmap of deliverables
changes.now: A new Roadmap tab (key 6) shows what we plan to ship, by workstream and time. The columns get coarser further out (this quarter, next quarter, halves, a year, Later), and a broad target is a wide card that narrows as you sharpen it. Drag a card to another time or workstream, or onto a Jira release to tie it to that release.

changes.title: Ideas in one line
changes.now: + Add idea takes just a name, stamped with the meeting it came from (today's meeting by default), and lands in Ideas to sort. One click picks when it might ship. It's a quick update, so anyone can add ideas during the meeting without Start editing.

changes.title: Deliverables
changes.now: A deliverable is something we'll ship, in words a customer would understand: a name, release-note wording, a kind (New, Improved, Fixed), a target that sharpens from a year to a quarter to a Jira release or date, a workstream, owners, tags and notes. Stages are Idea, Planned (automatic once it has a target), Done and Dropped (with a reason).

changes.title: Deliverables link to Jira work
changes.now: Link one or more Jira issues, features or epics to a deliverable, and progress rolls up ("3 of 5 linked Jira issues done"), counting each issue once. In Manage, Jira work, pick epics or stories and choose Group into a deliverable. Links never change Jira.
changes.where: A deliverable's card; Manage, Jira work.

changes.title: Badges and nudges
changes.now: Cards show In Jira, Needs detail (with the reason, such as pick a quarter as it comes into view, add an owner, link the Jira work), At risk (past its target, or little done close to it) and Ready for release notes (Done, with its Jira release). Split turns a broad deliverable into smaller ones.

headline: Clearer names: Sprint, Manage, Jira work

changes.title: Sprint and Manage
changes.now: The Cards tab is now Sprint: the current Jira sprint's work. The Plan tab is now Manage: Jira work, the team, the lists and setup. Keys 1 to 5 still go to the same places.

changes.title: Jira work and Timeboxes
changes.now: In Manage, Epics is now Jira work (it holds stories too), and Sprints is now Timeboxes: Jira's sprints, then the plan's own timeboxes after them, each marked Jira sprint or Plan timebox.

changes.title: All sources, Jira only, Jira + mine
changes.now: The layer buttons now say what they show: All sources (Jira and everything added here), Jira only, and Jira + mine (Jira plus what you added). Mine elsewhere means work assigned to you or owned by you.

changes.title: One meaning of release
changes.now: Release means a Jira release. The Scrum pack's release block is now Release day (a plan that already has Release keeps it), and What's new is What's new in Sightline, so it isn't mistaken for your own release notes.

headline: A compact capacity widget

changes.title: Capacity takes less room
changes.now: With more than 8 people, Capacity lists only who's over or close to capacity, with a line per sprint (for example, 1 over, 2 close, 12 within) and Show all to see everyone; your choice is remembered. Once the team capacity is set it's one line with Change, and rows are tighter.

headline: The page is now sightline.html

changes.title: The page file is named sightline.html
changes.now: The shared page is now sightline.html, with sightline.html.sha256 beside it, and the copy instructions say so. Your saved settings, who you are and your linked plan carry over; nothing needs setting up again.
changes.where: The page file; the damaged-copy message.

headline: Senior review 11: Saved means saved

changes.title: Save as you go says Saved only when it saved
changes.now: A change a rule refuses (like a workstream blackout) stays unsaved on screen instead of being reported saved. If a teammate deleted what you changed, your version downloads as a backup. When a teammate starts editing, your change waits and says so. After a failed save it waits longer before each retry.

changes.title: Nothing doubles or overwrites in a race
changes.now: Two people adding team capacity on different dates both keep theirs. Putting stories or epics on the board, and setting team capacity, are worked out again on the latest file when someone saves at the same moment, so a story is never placed twice.

changes.title: Bulk stories keep your picks
changes.now: Picked stories stay picked while you filter, and the bar says how many are hidden by the filter. Pick all says how many it picks, including any beyond the 300 listed. If a bulk save doesn't land, the stories stay picked. The Epics filter redraws after a short pause, which keeps big lists fast.

changes.title: Cards and capacity read right
changes.now: Someone at 0% (or away all sprint) with assigned work shows against zero, as over. The team capacity figure can be removed, and Set never sticks on Saving. Jira work assigned to someone not linked here gets a row with their name and a Link action. Pull requests say when coverage was partial even with none found, and when the list is cut to 100.

changes.title: Faster with big teams
changes.now: Jira user pickers show their best few choices and fill in the rest when opened, instead of building tens of thousands of options. Today's count no longer searches every task for each task on every keystroke.

changes.title: The pull request time limit holds
changes.now: After its two-minute limit, the sync keeps earlier pull request data, even if old, instead of asking Jira again, and it checks every page in the plan's folder for a newer Sightline.

headline: Put many stories on the board at once

changes.title: Put many stories on the board at once
changes.now: In Plan, Epics, stories in a sprint with no epic now have checkboxes and Pick all. Put the picked stories on one workstream, or each on its suggested workstream (where its assignee already has work), in one save. Stories with no suggestion stay picked so you can place them next.
changes.where: Plan, Epics, In a sprint, not on the board.

headline: Pull requests show their repository

changes.title: A Repository column for pull requests
changes.now: The pull request list on Cards has a Repository column (project/repo). The sync takes it from Jira's development panel, the target repository, or the pull request's Bitbucket address, so it shows even when Jira leaves the name out; files synced before this get it from the address too.

headline: Senior review 10: safer saving, truer capacity

changes.title: Save as you go never loses an edit
changes.now: If a Save as you go write fails, your edit stays on screen and unsaved, and it tries again. Turning it off saves any pending change first. A field left focused still saves after a pause. If a teammate changed the same thing since you started, yours is saved and theirs downloads as a backup.

changes.title: Merges are careful
changes.now: Merging changes only fields that hold people, never text that happens to match. If someone saves at the same moment, the merge is worked out again on the latest file, so new work isn't left with a missing owner. Merging away yourself keeps you as the person kept. Two Jira users with the same name are never offered as duplicates, and Merge all lists any Jira link it drops.

changes.title: Capacity counts what it should
changes.now: Team capacity now saves and merges like other changes. A company holiday takes a day off everyone's share, and a figure dated mid-sprint applies to that sprint. With a team figure, people without a Jira user are shown too. Each heat-map cell says in words whether it's within capacity or over, for screen readers. Deactivating counts open work Jira assigns them.

changes.title: Cards and burndown, more honest
changes.now: The burndown notes work added since the sprint started and doesn't count it as slipping, and an overdue sprint's last day uses resolved dates. A person filter keeps their Jira issues that aren't on the plan. Pull requests say when they were read for only some issues. Focus stays on the control you used, and with no Jira sprint yet one line says what to set up.

changes.title: Read-only quick controls work
changes.now: Allocation, team capacity and Jira linking in Plan, Team stay usable when you're not editing, as quick updates. Team and Jira users are drawn only when shown, which keeps large teams fast.

changes.title: Faster, clearer sync extras
changes.now: Reading pull requests stops after two minutes and records how many issues it covered. The newer-page check looks only at .html files. If the newer page has another name, the banner says to open that file instead of offering a refresh that wouldn't get it.

headline: Team capacity, with allocation

changes.title: Team capacity, set from a date
changes.now: Set one figure for the team, points per person per sprint, and change it from a date when it changes. Each person's share is that figure times their allocation, less time off and holidays in the sprint. Each sprint column shows the figure in force. Plans without one still use each person's own points per sprint.

changes.title: Allocation
changes.now: Give someone who's partly on the team an allocation (for example 50%); their share of capacity follows it. Left blank, it follows their days per week. Set it in Plan, Team or right in the Capacity widget, without Start editing.

headline: Open a person from Plan, Team

changes.title: Names in Plan, Team open the person's card
changes.now: In Plan, Team a name now opens that person's card (Jira user, Merge into, Deactivate). While editing, an Open link sits beside the name box.

headline: Knows when there's a newer Sightline

changes.title: A newer Sightline? Refresh safely
changes.now: The page now says when a newer Sightline is available: a teammate saved the plan with a newer version, or the Jira sync found a newer page in the plan's folder. Refresh saves your unsaved edits first and ends editing; if the save fails or you cancel, the page stays open with your edits.

changes.title: The sync spots a newer page
changes.now: Each sync notes the newest Sightline page among the .html files in the plan's folder (only its version stamp and file name), so an open page can offer to refresh.

headline: Cards is Jira's sprint; outside owners

changes.title: Cards shows Jira's work only
changes.now: Cards now shows the active Jira sprint's issues, including ones not placed on the plan (marked Not on the plan; they open in Jira). Plan-only tasks and initiatives are left off, with a note that they're on Today and the Timeline.

changes.title: Outside owners
changes.now: Add a team, vendor or group (like Platform team) as an outside owner. It can own anything and be waited on, but has no capacity, time off or sprint load. Any owner field can pick one or add one on the spot, Waiting on lists them, and they get a row by person while they own open work.
changes.where: Plan, Team, Outside owners; any Owner field; Mark blocked.

headline: Merge duplicate people; faster linking

changes.title: Merge duplicate people
changes.now: If you typed a first name and later added the same person from Jira with their full name, merge them: their work, notes, blockers, meetings, groups, views, history, time off, capacity and Jira link move to the one kept, and the duplicate is removed. Plan, Team lists likely duplicates with Merge all; any person's card has Merge into.

changes.title: Link all suggested at once
changes.now: People, Jira users has Link all suggested, which links every suggested match in one save instead of one save each. Link, Unlink and Add to team buttons now show that they're working as soon as you click.

changes.title: Stopping a watch frees it at once
changes.now: Ctrl+C on watch now gives back its lock, so starting a new watch works straight away instead of saying one is already running. When one really is running, the message says which process, when it last checked in, and that it may be the minimized window that starts at sign-in.

headline: Deactivate people

changes.title: Deactivate someone who left the team
changes.now: Deactivate a person from Plan, Team or their card. They keep their history (past owners, notes, their Jira link) but leave owner pickers, Cards rows, load, capacity and meetings' Everyone. While they still own open work, they keep a row by person, flagged so it gets reassigned. Reactivate any time from Team, Inactive.

headline: Cards reads at a glance; add sprints through a date

changes.title: A sprint header you can read at a glance
changes.now: Cards now opens with the sprint's name (without the dates in it), its dates, tiles for to do, in progress, done and blocked, and a bar for how far in it is. The burndown leads with points left and how far ahead of or behind the ideal line you are, and marks Today.

changes.title: Capacity as a heat map
changes.now: Capacity is now a heat map: each cell is shaded by load against what the person can take (under 70%, on target, over, 30%+ over), or by relative load where that isn't set. Numbers no longer repeat "pts", and setting points per sprint is a quick update.

changes.title: Add sprints through a date
changes.now: Pick a date under the sprint list and Sightline adds sprints of the default length, named on from the last one, until one reaches it. It says how many it will add before you click.

changes.title: Link Jira users without Start editing
changes.now: Linking a person to their Jira user, or adding a Jira user to the team, is now a quick update that works read-only. The Team tab has a Jira user column to link from there too, and capacity's unlinked row links straight to People.
changes.where: Plan, Team; People, Jira users; a person's card.

changes.title: Clearer sprint days, tidier lists
changes.now: "5 of 10 days in" now reads "working day 5 of 10", or "5 of 10 working days done" on a weekend or holiday, and the top bar follows Jira's active sprint as Cards does. A release's issue list is one left-aligned line each, and the Jira users table fits its content.
changes.where: The top bar, Cards, a release's card, People.

changes.title: The demo shows releases, pull requests and burndown
changes.now: tools/make-demo.py now writes Jira releases, pull requests from the development panel, burndown notes, created, updated and comment dates, and points per sprint, so every Cards widget and the release cards show without a Jira.

headline: Cards widgets line up

changes.title: Burndown, capacity and pull requests as widgets
changes.now: On Cards, the burndown, capacity and pull requests are now widgets of one shape in one grid: aligned, with the same header, and the chart fills its widget instead of floating in a wide box.

changes.title: One sprint, and the right points left
changes.now: Cards now follows Jira's active sprint, as the burndown does, instead of the plan's own sprint dates. Points left counts stories that are done now as done, even without a resolved date.

headline: pull requests from Bitbucket

changes.title: Pull requests on Cards
changes.now: Cards now has an Open pull requests panel for the sprint's open work: each PR's repository, author, when it was last updated and how many reviewers approved, oldest first, with the ones waiting 3+ days called out. Cards can show a PRs field, and a quick filter finds work with a PR waiting.

changes.title: A Jira item's pull requests
changes.now: A Jira item's card now lists its pull requests, with links to Bitbucket.

changes.title: The sync reads pull requests
changes.now: For the active sprint's open work, the sync reads pull requests from Jira's development panel, with your Jira token: no Bitbucket token or setup. It rereads at most every 30 minutes, and stops asking if your Jira has no development panel. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py.

headline: Save as you go

changes.title: Save as you go
changes.now: Turn on Save as you go (in the bar above the timeline) to edit without Start editing: each change saves on its own a moment after you stop, and teammates' changes merge in, the way quick updates do. Two people can edit at once. Undo works on what's saved. It waits while someone else has Start editing. It's per person, in this browser; turn it off to go back to Start editing.

headline: review: smoother, safer, clearer

changes.title: Nothing lost in a merge or an older copy
changes.now: Saved card views now merge with a teammate's save instead of being dropped, and come back with Put them back. A saved view's zoom and an edited update are named for older copies, so those open the plan read-only instead of dropping them.

changes.title: Blackouts hold, and typing is light
changes.now: A change that the automatic scheduling would push into a workstream's blackout is refused. Typing a title no longer reschedules the plan or redraws the timeline: the chart's label updates as you type.

changes.title: Scrolling doesn't redraw
changes.now: Workstreams leaving or entering the dates on screen are shown and hidden in place as you scroll, without redrawing the timeline.
changes.where: The timeline, zoomed in or in Days.

changes.title: Sprints and numbers you can trust
changes.now: A long gap before Jira's first sprint no longer pulls Jira's sprints earlier. Abandoned work is left out of the burndown and capacity, and said; the sync reads statuses the way the plan does. Capacity names work assigned to people not linked here. Cards uses Jira's active sprint when the plan's sprints don't cover today.

changes.title: Smaller touches
changes.now: Saved card views keep the layout and leave your quick filters yours. Fit covers gates and releases. Releases are in Find and their issues open. Move its work checks first and says what doesn't fit. Pasted tags save as one change. Activity shows the newest 50 at a time. The parked note returns when different work is parked. New Year's observed on Dec 31 is included.

headline: card views, quick filters and aging

changes.title: Card views
changes.now: Lay out Cards by person, workstream or epic, and pick what each card shows: points, epic, how old it is, when it was last updated, and when it last got a comment, from Jira. Save a layout as a view for the team.

changes.title: Quick filters
changes.now: Narrow the cards with quick filters, like Jira's: mine, unassigned, blocked, not estimated, updated in 2 days, no update in 7+ days, or one person's. They're yours, separate from the saved layout, and the board says how many they hide.

changes.title: The sync reads last comments
changes.now: For the issues on Cards (this and coming sprints) the sync reads when each last got a comment, in small batches. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py; no new options.

headline: sprint burndown and capacity in points

changes.title: Sprint burndown
changes.now: Cards now shows a burndown for the active Jira sprint: points left each working day against the ideal line, with today marked. It uses each story's resolved date, and the sync's daily notes where it has them, which also show scope added mid-sprint. It says how many stories aren't estimated.

changes.title: Capacity, in points
changes.now: A capacity grid shows each person's points in Jira for this and the next sprints against their points per sprint, less their time off and holidays; over is red. Set each person's points per sprint right in the grid.

changes.title: The sync keeps a daily burndown note
changes.now: Each sync notes the active sprint's points in scope and points left for the day, and reads each issue's created and resolved dates. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py; no new options.

headline: workstream blackouts

changes.title: Blackouts outside a workstream's dates
changes.now: Before a workstream starts and after it ends is now a striped blackout. Making or moving the plan's own initiatives, tasks or milestones into it is refused with the reason, and the + to add doesn't appear there. Work already there when you set the dates stays, shown in the blackout.
changes.where: Workstreams with start or end dates.

changes.title: Jira work and a workstream's dates
